title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
誰與歸
考試官教諭劉　批〔此論有抑揚有關鍵表武侯事於青天白日之下讀之令人竦然其亦知所期待者歟試百以俟〕
考試官學正方　批〔豪邁而不違準繩馳驟而不至窘步蓋學古作而得其要領者矣〕
立言有要而相道得焉其垂法也遠矣甚哉相
道之難也得其道而垂法於後世者爲其誠也
爲其公也爲其樂取於人而不自用也否則矯
強於詐力之末固蔽於有我之私訑訑然距人
===
於千里之外適足以病天下矣抑將焉用彼相
哉而何以爲萬世相天下者之法哉請申吳氏
之言而繹其旨乾稱父坤稱母大君者吾父母
之宗子大臣宗子之家相也黃帝堯舜禹之相
得其道而天下理固無容議矣伊尹之相湯傅
說之相高宗周公之相成王其謨訓功烈亦可
以爲萬世法矣後之相者或挾知謀以欺天下
或徇私意以愚天下或拒諫飾非以輕天下之
數者固不知爲相之體也亦不足爲相之法
punctuated:
誰與歸？

考試官教諭劉，批〔此論有抑揚，有關鍵，表武侯事於青天白日之下，讀之令人竦然。其亦知所期待者歟？試百以俟。〕

考試官學正方，批〔豪邁而不違準繩，馳驟而不至窘步，蓋學古作而得其要領者矣。〕

立言有要，而相道得焉，其垂法也遠矣。甚哉，相道之難也！得其道而垂法於後世者，爲其誠也，爲其公也，爲其樂取於人而不自用也。否則，矯強於詐力之末，固蔽於有我之私，訑訑然距人於千里之外，適足以病天下矣。抑將焉用彼相哉？而何以爲萬世相天下者之法哉？請申吳氏之言而繹其旨。乾稱父，坤稱母，大君者吾父母之宗子，大臣宗子之家相也。黃帝、堯、舜、禹之相，得其道而天下理，固無容議矣。伊尹之相湯，傅說之相高宗，周公之相成王，其謨訓功烈亦可以爲萬世法矣。後之相者，或挾知謀以欺天下，或徇私意以愚天下，或拒諫飾非以輕天下。之數者固不知爲相之體也，亦不足爲相之法。
translation_en:
…with whom should I find fellowship?

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “This discourse has measured emphasis and clear pivotal points. It brings the deeds of the Marquis of Wu into the full light of day; reading it inspires awe. Does its author also understand what is expected of him? ‘Test a hundred and await’ [?].”

Examiner Fang, School Director, comments: “Bold and expansive, yet never departing from established standards; swift in its course, yet never stumbling: this is surely the work of someone who has studied ancient compositions and grasped their essentials.”\n
When a statement grasps the essentials, the Way of serving as chief councillor is apprehended through it, and the example it transmits reaches far. How difficult is the Way of the chief councillor! Those who attain this Way and transmit an example to later generations do so through their sincerity, their impartiality, and their delight in learning from others rather than relying solely on themselves. Otherwise, exerting themselves through the petty devices of deceit and force, hemmed in by selfish attachment to their own views, and arrogantly keeping others a thousand li away, they merely bring suffering upon the realm. What use, then, could there be for such chief councillors? How could they provide a model for those who serve as chief councillors of the realm throughout all ages? Allow me to expand upon Master Wu’s words and unfold their meaning. Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother. The sovereign is the principal heir of our father and mother; the great ministers are the stewards of that heir’s household. The chief councillors of Huangdi, Yao, Shun, and Yu attained this Way, and the realm was well governed: there is assuredly no room for dispute about this. As for Yi Yin’s service as chief councillor to Tang, Fu Yue’s to Gaozong, and the Duke of Zhou’s to King Cheng, their counsels, instructions, and achievements likewise furnish models for all ages. Among later chief councillors, some used their clever schemes to deceive the realm; some followed their private inclinations to keep the realm in ignorance; and some rejected remonstrance and glossed over their errors, treating the realm with contempt. These several types [?] certainly did not understand the essential character of service as chief councillor, nor are they worthy to serve as models for it.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
孔明之相蜀也以興復漢室爲已任以鞠躬盡
瘁而自許豈不謂挾智徇私者可以取天下而
不可以服天下拒諫飾非者徒以輕天下而不
可以安天下孰若開誠布公會衆善而補吾闕
耶激勸者天下之大柄也必開誠心布公道以
天下之是非爲去取則循名責實虛僞不齒而
有以服天下之心矣自用者天下之至愚也必
集衆思廣忠益以天下之耳目爲視聽則以虛
受人不自滿假而有以來天下之善矣文過者
===
天下之鄙吝也必以入之忠慮而攻吾之闕失
則勞謙終吉噬膚有慶而足以充天下之量矣
孔明之所以自盡而布告於人人者蓋如此故
盡忠益時者雖讎必賞犯法怠慢者雖親必罰
服罪輸情者雖重必釋游辭巧飾者雖輕必戮
發乎至誠之心也昭乎至公之道也以是道而
相天下萬世可法也慕徐元直之啓誨嘉董幼
宰之違反容胡濟之獻納謝楊顒之陳諫謀思
之必精也忠益之不遺也以是道而相天下萬
punctuated: 孔明之相蜀也，以興復漢室爲已任，以鞠躬盡瘁而自許。豈不謂挾智徇私者可以取天下，而不可以服天下；拒諫飾非者徒以輕天下，而不可以安天下？孰若開誠布公，會衆善而補吾闕耶？激勸者，天下之大柄也。必開誠心，布公道，以天下之是非爲去取，則循名責實，虛僞不齒，而有以服天下之心矣。自用者，天下之至愚也。必集衆思，廣忠益，以天下之耳目爲視聽，則以虛受人，不自滿假，而有以來天下之善矣。文過者，天下之鄙吝也。必以入之忠慮而攻吾之闕失，則勞謙終吉，噬膚有慶，而足以充天下之量矣。孔明之所以自盡而布告於人人者，蓋如此。故盡忠益時者，雖讎必賞；犯法怠慢者，雖親必罰；服罪輸情者，雖重必釋；游辭巧飾者，雖輕必戮。發乎至誠之心也，昭乎至公之道也。以是道而相天下，萬世可法也。慕徐元直之啓誨，嘉董幼宰之違反，容胡濟之獻納，謝楊顒之陳諫，謀思之必精也，忠益之不遺也。以是道而相天下，萬
translation_en: When Kongming served as chief minister of Shu, he took the restoration of the Han ruling house as his own responsibility and pledged to exert himself to the utmost until utterly spent. Surely he believed that those who wield cunning and pursue private interests might seize the realm but could not win its allegiance, and that those who reject remonstrance and gloss over their faults merely treat the realm lightly and cannot bring it peace. How could these approaches compare with displaying sincerity and impartiality, gathering the good in others to remedy one’s own shortcomings? Encouragement is a great instrument for governing the realm. One must reveal a sincere heart, uphold impartial principles, and base acceptance and rejection on the rights and wrongs recognized throughout the realm. Then one can demand actual performance corresponding to professed qualifications, exclude the false and hypocritical, and win the hearts of all under Heaven. Trusting only one’s own judgment is the greatest folly in the world. One must gather the thoughts of many and broaden the benefits of loyal counsel, taking the eyes and ears of all under Heaven as one’s own means of seeing and hearing. Then one can receive others with an open mind, without self-satisfaction or conceit, and attract the good of the realm. Concealing one’s faults is the basest narrow-mindedness in the world. One must use others’ loyal counsel [?] to correct one’s shortcomings and errors. Then, as the Book of Changes says, ‘Toiling with humility brings good fortune in the end,’ and ‘Biting through skin brings blessings’; one’s capacity will thus suffice to embrace the realm. Such, broadly, were the principles by which Kongming devoted himself fully to his duties and which he proclaimed to everyone. Thus, those who gave their utmost loyalty and benefited their age were invariably rewarded, even if they were his enemies; those who broke the law or neglected their duties were invariably punished, even if they were his relatives. Those who admitted their guilt and disclosed the facts were invariably pardoned, even for grave offenses; those who used evasive words and clever embellishments were invariably executed, even for minor offenses. This sprang from a heart of utmost sincerity and manifested the way of utmost impartiality. To serve as chief minister of the realm according to this way provides a model for ten thousand generations. He valued Xu Yuanzhi’s enlightening instruction, commended Dong Youzai’s dissent, welcomed Hu Ji’s advice, and thanked Yang Yong for his remonstrances. His deliberations were invariably thorough, and he overlooked no benefit offered by loyal counsel. To serve as chief minister of the realm according to this way provides a model for ten thousand…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
世可法也考微勞徵壯烈善則稱人過則稱己
也引咎責躬布所失於天下善則稱君過則稱
已也以是道而相天下萬世可法也是則孔明
之功業未究而其言為相之法萬世可傳必有
以得其體要而中其肯綮者矣視彼挾智徇私
拒諫飾非適足以病天下者烏可同日而語哉
孔明其何以致此耶方其高卧隆中寧靜致遠
王佐之才固已素定於胸中矣及其起而相蜀
也前定之言出而為籍曰誠也曰公也曰忠益
===
也曰忠慮也是卽伊尹脩身允德無自廣以狹
人之說也是卽傅說王恍不難官不及私昵之
說也是卽周公作周孚先丕視功載而受人微
言者之說也孔明之言有以該之孰謂其不足
為萬世相天下者之法哉是故孔明之言為法
於萬世固也彼新莽孔光王安石之流吾惑焉
自其人之誠心未開也雖謙恭下士而終不免
於偽自其人之公道未布也雖坐語移日而終
不免於私自其人之略衆思沮忠益而自處之
punctuated: 世可法也。考微勞，徵壯烈，善則稱人，過則稱己也；引咎責躬，布所失於天下，善則稱君，過則稱已也。以是道而相天下，萬世可法也。是則孔明之功業未究，而其言為相之法，萬世可傳，必有以得其體要而中其肯綮者矣。視彼挾智徇私、拒諫飾非，適足以病天下者，烏可同日而語哉？孔明其何以致此耶？方其高卧隆中，寧靜致遠，王佐之才固已素定於胸中矣。及其起而相蜀也，前定之言出而為籍，曰誠也，曰公也，曰忠益也，曰忠慮也。是卽伊尹脩身允德、無自廣以狹人之說也；是卽傅說王恍不難、官不及私昵之說也；是卽周公作周孚先、丕視功載而受人微言者之說也。孔明之言有以該之，孰謂其不足為萬世相天下者之法哉？是故孔明之言為法於萬世，固也。彼新莽、孔光、王安石之流，吾惑焉。自其人之誠心未開也，雖謙恭下士，而終不免於偽；自其人之公道未布也，雖坐語移日，而終不免於私；自其人之略衆思、沮忠益而自處之
translation_en:
…generations may take it as their model. He assessed even minor services and brought outstanding deeds to light, crediting others with what was good and himself with what was wrong. He accepted blame, reproached himself, and made his failings known throughout the realm, crediting his ruler with what was good and himself with what was wrong. To serve as chief minister of the realm in this way is to provide a model for ten thousand generations. Thus, although Kongming’s achievements remained incomplete, his words constitute a model for chief ministers that may be transmitted for ten thousand generations. Surely he grasped the essential principles of the office and struck at its crucial points. How could he be mentioned in the same breath as those who exploit their cleverness to pursue private interests, reject remonstrance, and gloss over their errors, thereby bringing nothing but harm upon the realm?

How did Kongming attain this? While he lived in retirement at Longzhong, pursuing far-reaching aims through tranquility, his capacity to assist a king was already firmly established within him. When he emerged to serve as chief minister of Shu, the principles he had settled upon beforehand were expressed in words and committed to writing: sincerity, impartiality, loyal service that benefits the ruler, and loyal deliberation [?]. These are precisely Yi Yin’s teachings about cultivating oneself and making one’s virtue true, without magnifying oneself so as to belittle others. They are precisely Fu Yue’s teachings that “the king, in a state of bewilderment, finds no difficulty [?]” and that official appointments must not extend to personal favorites. They are precisely the Duke of Zhou’s teachings about serving Zhou and taking trustworthiness as the foremost principle [?], giving great consideration to accomplished service, and accepting others’ subtle admonitions. Kongming’s words encompass these teachings. Who could say that they are inadequate as a model for those who serve as chief ministers of the realm throughout ten thousand generations?

That Kongming’s words should serve as a model for ten thousand generations is therefore beyond doubt. As for the likes of Wang Mang of Xin, Kong Guang, and Wang Anshi, I have my doubts. Because their sincerity had never unfolded, even though they were humble and respectful toward men of learning, they ultimately could not escape hypocrisy. Because their impartiality had never been put into practice, even though they sat in discussion for hours, they ultimately could not escape self-interest. Because they disregarded the thinking of others and thwarted loyal efforts to benefit the ruler, while their own stance…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
不廣也雖借口堯舜之道終亦不免於偏而流
禍天下玆固未識相體者之所爲也而謂法孔
明以盡其道者爲乎哉雖然孔明知爲相之體
矣其感楊顒之諫生旣謝之死又哀之豈不知
其言之忠哉然而食少事繁若不知愛其身者
未可以常情窺淺見議也彼大廈𢡖幪而震風
凌雨適與壞會亟假乎一木之支則公輸子必
自絜之而躬爲之弗徐徐以鳩衆工矣孔明之
時勢何異於是哉遠邇細大靡不究心夫豈可
===
已而不已者三分割據志決身殲天地鬼神實
臨之矣噫孔明之所能者人也其所不能者天
也然則君子豈可以成敗論人物哉
表
擬宋以富弼爲司空侍中平章事謝表〔熙〕
寧二年
季方
同考試官教諭王　批〔寓駢儷於渾厚中可録以〕
式後學
punctuated:
不廣也，雖借口堯舜之道，終亦不免於偏，而流禍天下。玆固未識相體者之所爲也，而謂法孔明以盡其道者爲乎哉？雖然，孔明知爲相之體矣。其感楊顒之諫，生旣謝之，死又哀之，豈不知其言之忠哉？然而食少事繁，若不知愛其身者，未可以常情窺、淺見議也。彼大廈𢡖幪，而震風凌雨適與壞會，亟假乎一木之支，則公輸子必自絜之，而躬爲之，弗徐徐以鳩衆工矣。孔明之時勢何異於是哉？遠邇細大，靡不究心，夫豈可已而不已者？三分割據，志決身殲，天地鬼神實臨之矣。噫！孔明之所能者，人也；其所不能者，天也。然則君子豈可以成敗論人物哉？

表
擬宋以富弼爲司空侍中平章事謝表〔熙〕寧二年
季方

同考試官教諭王　批〔寓駢儷於渾厚中，可録以〕式後學。
translation_en:
…their outlook was not broad. Though they invoked the Way of Yao and Shun, they ultimately could not escape partiality and brought calamity upon the realm. Such conduct indeed belonged to men who did not understand the proper role of a chief minister. Could it be called emulating Kongming and fully carrying out his way?

Nevertheless, Kongming understood the proper role of a chief minister. Moved by Yang Yong’s remonstrance, he thanked him while he lived and mourned him after his death. How could he have failed to recognize the loyalty of his words? Yet he ate little and attended to many affairs, seemingly without regard for his own health. This cannot be fathomed through ordinary feelings or judged with shallow insight. Suppose a great mansion stands gloom-shrouded [?], and violent winds and driving rain strike just as it is about to collapse, urgently requiring a single timber to prop it up. Master Gongshu would surely take its measure himself and personally undertake the work, rather than leisurely assemble a company of craftsmen. How did Kongming’s circumstances differ from this? He devoted his utmost attention to everything, near and far, small and great. Could these have been efforts he might have ceased but refused to cease? With the realm divided among three contending powers, his resolve was fixed, and he gave his life. Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits were indeed witnesses to it. Alas! What lay within Kongming’s power was human effort; what lay beyond it was Heaven. How, then, could a gentleman judge men by success or failure?

Memorial
A memorial of thanks, composed in the person of Fu Bi upon his appointment under the Song as Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, and Grand Councilor, in the second year of Xining [1069].
By Ji Fang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “It incorporates parallel phrasing within a substantial and harmonious style. It merits inclusion as a model for later students.”

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉　批〔表佳〕
考試官學正方　批〔典則〕
伏以
官司邦事治水土而總工虞職典朝儀導
輿輅而親帷幄秉鈞當軸論道經邦玆三
秩之俱崇乃一時而並拜
天心屬眷氷簴戰兢戴巨鼇之山未如
恩重泛大鯨之海秪覺䰟驚顧常伯親臣必達
周公之訓越冬官重任須資伯禹之才位
既極於阿衡人必擇乎亮采伏念臣學惟
===
窺豹才匪屠龍肆惟天聖之
朝偶中茂才之選初知
制誥贊
廟堂無鳳翥之文再使契丹靖沙漠乏鷹揚
之武荷
帝心之簡任辭樞副而未能竊附仲淹志四海
太平之治見傾夏竦忘一身譽毀之私發
官廩以賑饑功惟尺寸厘皇華而增秩
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉　批〔表佳〕
考試官學正方　批〔典則〕
伏以，官司邦事，治水土而總工虞；職典朝儀，導輿輅而親帷幄；秉鈞當軸，論道經邦。玆三秩之俱崇，乃一時而並拜。天心屬眷，氷簴戰兢。戴巨鼇之山，未如恩重；泛大鯨之海，秪覺䰟驚。顧常伯親臣，必達周公之訓；越冬官重任，須資伯禹之才。位既極於阿衡，人必擇乎亮采。
伏念臣學惟窺豹，才匪屠龍。肆惟天聖之朝，偶中茂才之選。初知制誥，贊廟堂，無鳳翥之文；再使契丹，靖沙漠，乏鷹揚之武。荷帝心之簡任，辭樞副而未能。竊附仲淹，志四海太平之治；見傾夏竦，忘一身譽毀之私。發官廩以賑饑，功惟尺寸；厘皇華而增秩，
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔A fine memorial.〕
Examiner Fang, School Director, comments: 〔Canonical and proper.〕
I humbly submit: one office oversees the affairs of the realm, regulating waters and lands and directing the officials responsible for public works and natural resources; another governs court ceremonial, guiding the imperial carriage and serving close to Your Majesty’s private councils; another holds the balance of government at its pivotal point, expounding the Way and ordering the state. These three ranks are all exalted, yet I have received appointment to all three at once. Your Majesty has bestowed your favor upon me, and I tremble in apprehension [?]. Even the mountain borne by the giant turtle is less weighty than your grace; as though afloat upon a sea of great whales, I feel only terror in my soul. Those who serve as senior ministers and intimate attendants must comprehend the Duke of Zhou’s teachings; the weighty responsibilities of the winter office require the talents of Yu the Great. Since these positions reach the eminence of Yi Yin’s chief ministership, those selected must be capable of faithfully accomplishing their duties.
I humbly reflect that my learning offers only a glimpse of the leopard, and my abilities fall short of the art of slaying dragons. During the Tiansheng reign, I happened to be selected in the examination for outstanding talent. First, as Drafter of Proclamations, I assisted the court, though my writing lacked the soaring grace of a phoenix. Twice I went as envoy to the Khitan to pacify the desert frontier, though I lacked the martial prowess of a soaring hawk. Honored by Your Majesty’s personal selection, I sought unsuccessfully to decline appointment as Vice Military Affairs Commissioner. I ventured to associate myself with Zhongyan, aspiring to bring peace and good government throughout the realm. When Xia Song sought my downfall, I set aside personal concern for praise or blame. I opened the government granaries to relieve famine, though my achievement was slight; through conducting imperial missions, I gained promotion …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
寵異尋常懇上封章繆有唐子房之論薦超遷
相位以隨文彥博以同升求解樞機止緣
一疾幸膺使相得判兩州自分樗材宜置
寬閒之野敢懷
楓詔荐優遲暮之年玆蓋伏遇
○○○○
謙恭孝友
勤儉聰明耿光近麗於
祖宗大化遠追乎堯舜遊畋罔御緝敬止於文
===
王宮室匪崇紹祗台於大禹
天章渙汗驚俯畀乎儒紳
聖學離明華親降乎館閣第臣力微任大罔知
圖報之因而
恩重身輕誓守致忠之願運一心以籌衆職竭
千慮以攄寸長祠祀惟清出納惟允撫四
夷熙庶績期奮百揆之庸亮天地理陰陽
冀補
九重之袞伏願對揚篤敘宣
punctuated:
寵異尋常。懇上封章，繆有唐子房之論薦；超遷相位，以隨文彥博以同升。求解樞機，止緣一疾；幸膺使相，得判兩州。自分樗材，宜置寬閒之野；敢懷楓詔，荐優遲暮之年。玆蓋伏遇○○○○，謙恭孝友，勤儉聰明。耿光近麗於祖宗，大化遠追乎堯舜。遊畋罔御，緝敬止於文王；宮室匪崇，紹祗台於大禹。天章渙汗，驚俯畀乎儒紳；聖學離明，華親降乎館閣。

第臣力微任大，罔知圖報之因；而恩重身輕，誓守致忠之願。運一心以籌衆職，竭千慮以攄寸長。祠祀惟清，出納惟允。撫四夷，熙庶績，期奮百揆之庸；亮天地，理陰陽，冀補九重之袞。伏願對揚篤敘，宣
translation_en:
…the favor was beyond the ordinary. Earnest sealed memorials were submitted on my behalf, and Tang Zifang recommended me with undeserved praise. Promoted out of turn to the position of grand councilor, I followed Wen Yanbo, rising together with him. I sought release from responsibility for military affairs solely because of an illness; fortunately, I received appointment as military commissioner with the honorary title of grand councilor and was entrusted with administering two prefectures. I considered myself as useless as the timber of the tree of heaven, fit to be placed in some quiet, unoccupied retreat. How could I have imagined that an imperial summons would again confer gracious favor upon my declining years?

This has come about because I have humbly encountered ○○○○, modest and respectful, filial and affectionate toward brothers, diligent and frugal, perceptive and wise. Your radiant virtue rivals that of your imperial ancestors in the nearer past, while your great transforming influence reaches back to Yao and Shun. You do not indulge in excursions and hunting, continuing King Wen’s unwavering reverence; you do not exalt palace building, carrying forward the Great Yu’s reverence for the sovereign above. Your imperial writings flow forth like an irrevocable decree: we marvel that you graciously bestow them upon the scholarly officials. Your sagely learning shines like the sun, bringing splendor through your personal visits to the scholarly institutes and pavilions.

Yet my abilities are slight and my responsibilities great, and I know no means of repaying you. Your favor is weighty and my own life of little account; I swear to hold fast to my resolve to render loyal service. With undivided purpose I shall deliberate upon the many duties of office, exhausting every consideration to put my small abilities to use. I shall ensure purity in sacrifices and trustworthiness in receiving and issuing commands. Pacifying the peoples of the four quarters and bringing the many undertakings to fruition, I hope to exert myself in the work of directing all affairs; assisting Heaven and Earth and regulating yin and yang, I hope to mend the imperial robe—to remedy shortcomings in your government. I humbly wish to respond to and extol your favor, earnestly sustain the proper order, and proclaim…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
重光而日新
戩穀盤宜荷
百祿而天保
弘文耀武華西海之金甌謹始成終延萬年
之寶命臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策五道
第一問
考試官教諭劉　批〔聖王之道載諸六經要之萬世哉〕
鍾錫
朝
列聖之與與之脗合而無間矣此策鋪張揚厲燦燦可觀其涵泳
聖化而善鳴治道者歟
考試官學正方　批〔條答不遺自是作手〕
punctuated:
重光而日新，戩穀盤宜，荷百祿而天保。弘文耀武，華西海之金甌；謹始成終，延萬年之寶命。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策五道
第一問

考試官教諭劉，批〔聖王之道載諸六經，要之萬世哉〕
鍾錫
朝列聖之與與之脗合而無間矣。此策鋪張揚厲，燦燦可觀，其涵泳聖化而善鳴治道者歟？
考試官學正方，批〔條答不遺，自是作手〕
translation_en:
…renewing day by day the radiance of successive reigns; may blessings and good fortune be firmly established [?], and may Heaven protect you as you receive its hundred blessings. Promote civil accomplishments and display martial prowess, lending splendor to the golden vessel of the realm within the western seas [?]; take care at the beginning and bring matters to completion, prolonging the precious Mandate for ten thousand years. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The Way of the sage kings is recorded in the Six Classics; its essentials endure for ten thousand generations!〕

Zhong Xi

The successive sage sovereigns of the dynasty accord with it without the slightest gap [?]. This policy essay expounds its subject fully and vigorously; its brilliance is worthy of admiration. Is its author not one who has steeped himself in Your Majesty’s sagely transforming influence and can eloquently express the Way of governance?

Examiner Fang, School Instructor, comments: 〔His answers address every point without omission; he is clearly an accomplished writer.〕

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
前聖立極而治敎之迹見於經後聖繼出
而作述之功顯於古夫六經致治之迹聖
王所以脩道之敎也我
祖宗
列聖懋隆作述輝映千古先聖後聖其揆一也
詎不信哉知此則可以復明問矣何則結
繩之初未有文字也伏羲堯舜之立極而
易與書著與矣禹湯文武周公之繼出而
書詩禮濫觴矣若仲尼者異世同神而易
書詩禮春秋蓋金聲而玉振矣我
太祖高皇帝以武功定天下以文敎興太平條
成
===
大誥三編頒示天下其曰申明五常卽克綏厥
猷之旨也其曰爲民造福卽輯寧邦家之
心也其曰輕生易死復出
三誥以示之卽勿庸殺之姑惟敎之之意也孰
謂三編之旨有不同於書者乎
太宗文皇帝命儒臣編集性理大全一書首回
punctuated:
前聖立極，而治敎之迹見於經；後聖繼出，而作述之功顯於古。夫六經，致治之迹，聖王所以脩道之敎也。我祖宗列聖懋隆作述，輝映千古。先聖後聖，其揆一也，詎不信哉？知此則可以復明問矣。何則？結繩之初，未有文字也。伏羲堯舜之立極，而易與書著與矣；禹湯文武周公之繼出，而書詩禮濫觴矣。若仲尼者，異世同神，而易書詩禮春秋，蓋金聲而玉振矣。
我太祖高皇帝以武功定天下，以文敎興太平，條成《大誥》三編，頒示天下。其曰「申明五常」，卽「克綏厥猷」之旨也；其曰「爲民造福」，卽「輯寧邦家」之心也；其曰「輕生易死，復出三誥以示之」，卽「勿庸殺之，姑惟敎之」之意也。孰謂三編之旨有不同於書者乎？
太宗文皇帝命儒臣編集《性理大全》一書，首回
translation_en:
The former sages established the supreme standard, and the traces of their government and teaching appear in the classics; later sages arose in succession, and their achievements in creating and transmitting became manifest in antiquity. The Six Classics record the traces of achieving good government: they embody the teaching through which the sage kings cultivated the Way. Our ancestral emperors, sages all, magnificently advanced the work of creating and transmitting, casting their radiance across the ages. The former and later sages followed the same measure—is this not indeed true? Understanding this, we can answer your discerning question. Why is this so? In the earliest age, when knotted cords were used, there was as yet no writing. When Fu Xi, Yao, and Shun established the supreme standard, the Changes and the Documents emerged [?]; when Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou arose in succession, the Documents, Odes, and Rites had their beginnings. As for Zhongni [Confucius], although he lived in a different age, he shared their spiritual understanding. In his hands, the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals reached their consummation, like music opened by bronze bells and brought to completion by jade chimes.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao pacified All-under-Heaven through military achievement and brought forth an age of peace through cultural instruction. He compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three collections, arranging them in articles, and promulgated them throughout the realm. Their injunction to “clarify the Five Constant Virtues” expresses the purport of “securely ordering their ways.” Their call to “bring blessings to the people” expresses the intention to “bring harmony and peace to the state.” Their statement, “They hold life cheap and readily court death; therefore I issue the Three Pronouncements anew to instruct them,” expresses the meaning of “Do not put them to death; for now, simply teach them.” Who could claim that the purport of these three collections differs from that of the Documents?
Emperor Taizong Wen commanded his Confucian officials to compile the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli Daquan), beginning with the diagram [?]…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
說則主太極以著陰陽動靜之微次通書
則析元亨利貞以著天道通復之妙若西
銘則父母之名稱而乾坤之道得若太和
則形氣之言立而變化之理在孰謂性理
之要不有契於易者乎
宣宗章皇帝時則有五倫書謂至誠能贊天地
之化育裨道設教能致天下之觀化其敘
唐虞之事與典謨相合敘三代之事與訓
誥相符其於易書之要前人義固表裏兼
===
該矣
英宗睿皇帝時則有大明一統志上志星宿分
野下志山川物產則天地之文理著內志
京師爲四方之極外志方岳爲列郡之綱
則聖人之經畫明其與周官之體國經野
蓋損益沿革矣
憲宗純皇帝之續通鑑綱目書歲年時月而天
地運行之序周書善惡褒貶而聖人好惡
之志見蓋與春秋之屬辭比事相權衡也
punctuated:
說，則主太極以著陰陽動靜之微；次《通書》，則析元亨利貞以著天道通復之妙。若《西銘》，則父母之名稱，而乾坤之道得；若《太和》，則形氣之言立，而變化之理在。孰謂性理之要不有契於《易》者乎？
宣宗章皇帝時，則有《五倫書》，謂至誠能贊天地之化育，裨道設教能致天下之觀化。其敘唐虞之事，與典謨相合；敘三代之事，與訓誥相符。其於《易》《書》之要，前人義固表裏兼該矣。
英宗睿皇帝時，則有《大明一統志》。上志星宿分野，下志山川物產，則天地之文理著；內志京師爲四方之極，外志方岳爲列郡之綱，則聖人之經畫明。其與《周官》之體國經野，蓋損益沿革矣。
憲宗純皇帝之《續通鑑綱目》，書歲年時月，而天地運行之序周；書善惡褒貶，而聖人好惡之志見。蓋與《春秋》之屬辭比事相權衡也。
translation_en:
…the Explanation takes the Supreme Ultimate as its central principle to reveal the subtleties of yin and yang, movement and stillness. Next, Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu) analyzes origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy to reveal the wondrous workings of Heaven’s Way in its passage and return. In the Western Inscription (Ximing), the designations “father” and “mother” are invoked, and the Way of Heaven and Earth is thereby apprehended. In Great Harmony (Taihe), statements concerning form and vital energy are established, and the principles of transformation reside therein. Who could say that the essentials of nature and principle do not accord with the Book of Changes?
In the reign of Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, there was the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). It states that utmost sincerity can assist the transforming and nourishing activities of Heaven and Earth, and that supporting the Way and establishing instruction can bring all under Heaven to behold this transformation. Its accounts of the affairs of Tang and Yu accord with the “Canons” and “Counsels”; its accounts of the Three Dynasties accord with the “Instructions” and “Announcements.” In its treatment of the essentials of the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents, the meanings of earlier thinkers [?] are indeed comprehensively embraced, both outwardly and inwardly.
In the reign of Emperor Yingzong Rui, there was the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi). Above, it records the constellations and their corresponding terrestrial regions; below, it records mountains, rivers, and local products. Thus the patterns and principles of Heaven and Earth are made manifest. Within, it records the capital as the pivot of the four quarters; beyond, it records the regional authorities as the framework governing the prefectures. Thus the sage’s planning and organization are made clear. In relation to the establishment of the state and the demarcation of the countryside described in the Offices of Zhou, it represents adaptations through reduction and addition, continuity and change.
Emperor Xianzong Chun’s Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Xu Tongjian gangmu) records years, seasons, and months, fully presenting the sequence of Heaven and Earth’s movements. It records good and evil, praise and blame, revealing the sage’s intent in what he approves and condemns. It may thus be weighed alongside the Spring and Autumn Annals in its arrangement of wording and juxtaposition of events.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
大誥得禮之坊而足以安上治民性理得禮之
彝而可以著誠去僞五倫書圖天敘天秩
之典一統志寓卑高以陳之序則
列聖作述之書無非禮之貫通矣
大誥所以章志貞教而禁民之邪性理則以文
武周召爲詩之體五倫之脩身理家孰非
周南召南之義綱目之褒善貶惡同於緇
衣巷伯之情則
祖宗垂世之典罔非詩之訓迪矣
===
孝宗敬皇帝篤配天之玄德紹
烈祖之耿光
大明會典一書備三重之道貫五經之理宗統
元會而
昭代之制作巳兼補闕拾遺而萬世之法程
大備是又所謂集大成矣於戲莫爲於前
後將何繼莫爲於後前將曷傳即今日之
御製擬前古之遺經
聖祖
punctuated:
《大誥》得禮之坊，而足以安上治民；《性理》得禮之彝，而可以著誠去僞；《五倫書》圖天敘天秩之典，《一統志》寓卑高以陳之序，則列聖作述之書無非禮之貫通矣。
《大誥》所以章志貞教而禁民之邪；《性理》則以文武周召爲詩之體；《五倫》之脩身理家，孰非《周南》《召南》之義？《綱目》之褒善貶惡，同於《緇衣》《巷伯》之情，則祖宗垂世之典罔非詩之訓迪矣。
孝宗敬皇帝篤配天之玄德，紹烈祖之耿光。《大明會典》一書備三重之道，貫五經之理，宗統元會，而昭代之制作巳兼；補闕拾遺，而萬世之法程大備，是又所謂集大成矣。於戲！莫爲於前，後將何繼？莫爲於後，前將曷傳？即今日之御製，擬前古之遺經，聖祖
translation_en:
The Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) embodies the restraining barriers of ritual and thus suffices to secure those above and govern the people. Nature and Principle (Xingli) embodies the constant norms of ritual and can thus make sincerity manifest and eliminate falseness. The Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun Shu) depicts the ordinances of Heaven’s ordering of relationships and ranks; the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Unified Realm (Yitong Zhi) contains the ordered arrangement of low and high. Thus, the books composed and compiled by the successive sage emperors all embody the pervasive principles of ritual.
The Grand Pronouncements makes proper intentions manifest, establishes correct teaching, and restrains the people’s depravity. Nature and Principle takes Kings Wen and Wu and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao as the substance of the Odes. As for the cultivation of the person and ordering of the household in the Five Relationships, which of these does not embody the meaning of the “Airs of Zhou and the South” and the “Airs of Shao and the South”? The Outline and Details (Gangmu), in praising good and condemning evil, shares the sentiments of “Black Robes” and “Chief of the Palace Eunuchs.” Thus, the canonical works bequeathed to the world by the imperial ancestors all convey the instruction of the Odes.
Emperor Xiaozong Jing deepened his mysterious virtue, worthy to be matched with Heaven, and continued the radiant glory of his illustrious ancestors. The single work Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming Huidian) encompasses the Way of the three weighty tasks and runs through the principles of the Five Classics. Gathering their essentials into a unified whole, it comprehensively includes the institutions of this illustrious dynasty; supplying omissions and recovering what had been overlooked, it fully provides standards for all ages. This, too, is what is meant by bringing together a grand synthesis. Alas! If none had acted before, what could later generations continue? If none acted afterward, how could the achievements of earlier generations be transmitted? Taking the imperially authored works of today and comparing them with the classics handed down from antiquity, the sage ancestor …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
神孫功業相望
宸章奎翰日月爭光所以人文日盛治道日隆
斯民遷善遠罪日趨於蕩蕩平平之域與
唐虞三代之化異世而同功也豈區區漢
唐宋之治可與言哉愚也得與其進焉願
披露以揚厲無前之績謹對
第二問
王應奎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔求律呂於元聲元氣異乎膚〕
===
〔心於黍尺者矣宜錄〕
同考試官教諭趙　批〔鋪敘詳明是究心於律學者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔事有考據而文足以發之允宜高薦〕
考試官學正方　批〔以樂由於律而末復歸之功德〕
〔可謂知本〕
欲定黃鍾者當先求元聲欲得元聲者當
先候元氣夫聲無可據而氣有可驗也故
截管以候氣應氣以飛灰而元氣得矣元
氣得而黃鍾定矣黃鍾定而十二律生矣
punctuated:
神孫功業相望，宸章奎翰日月爭光，所以人文日盛，治道日隆，斯民遷善遠罪，日趨於蕩蕩平平之域，與唐虞三代之化異世而同功也。豈區區漢唐宋之治可與言哉？愚也得與其進焉，願披露以揚厲無前之績。謹對。

第二問
王應奎
同考試官訓導楊批〔求律呂於元聲元氣，異乎膚〕〔心於黍尺者矣，宜錄。〕
同考試官教諭趙批〔鋪敘詳明，是究心於律學者。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔事有考據，而文足以發之，允宜高薦。〕
考試官學正方批〔以樂由於律，而末復歸之功德，〕〔可謂知本。〕

欲定黃鍾者，當先求元聲；欲得元聲者，當先候元氣。夫聲無可據，而氣有可驗也。故截管以候氣，應氣以飛灰，而元氣得矣。元氣得而黃鍾定矣，黃鍾定而十二律生矣。
translation_en:
…the divine descendant’s achievements stand alongside those of his sagely forebear. His imperial writings and illustrious brushwork rival the sun and moon in brilliance. Thus cultural refinement flourishes daily, and the way of governance grows ever more exalted. The people turn toward goodness and distance themselves from wrongdoing, advancing daily toward a realm of broad and impartial order. Though belonging to a different age, this transformation matches the accomplishments of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties. How could the comparatively modest governance of the Han, Tang, and Song be mentioned alongside it? In my ignorance, I have been able to share in this progress, and wish to set forth my views to extol these unprecedented achievements. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Wang Yingkui
Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He seeks the pitch standards in the primal sound and primal qi, unlike those whose concern with millet grains and measuring rules is superficial [?]. He should be selected.〕
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition is detailed and clear; this is someone who has devoted himself to the study of pitch standards.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His points have documentary support, and his prose adequately elucidates them. He certainly deserves a high recommendation.〕
Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: 〔He takes music to derive from pitch standards, and at the end returns it to meritorious achievement and virtue. He may be said to understand the root.〕

To establish Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch, one must first seek the primal sound; to obtain the primal sound, one must first observe the primal qi. Sound offers no firm basis to rely on, whereas qi provides something that can be verified. Thus one cuts tubes to observe qi; when the ashes fly up in response to qi, the primal qi is ascertained. Once the primal qi is ascertained, Huangzhong is established. Once Huangzhong is established, the twelve pitch standards are generated.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
十二律生而五聲和矣五聲和可以被諸
八音而爲樂矣夫如是則凡八音之器其
輕重大小長短厚薄多寡盈縮之數皆本
之律其體則天地之體其用之和而能感
通天地也不亦宜哉粤自黄帝始命伶倫
造十二律之管吹陽律以候於鳳者六曰
黄鍾太簇姑洗蕤賓夷則無射是也吹陰
律以候於凰者六曰大吕夾鍾仲吕林鍾
南吕應鍾是也故能協和中聲候氣不爽
===
清濁相符倫理無失而後世之言律者實
肇於此唐虞三代弗可尚已自是而下制
作紛紛卒未有歸一之論以漢言之相統
之法三五不周畸羸之數損益不用京房
之見尚如此彼張蒼之輩又何足望也庶
幾者其司馬遷乎以唐言之梁陳之音采
而雜用周齊之技集而合作祖孝孫之見
尚如此彼魏延陵之徒又何足道也庶幾
者其張文收乎至於有宋之時雖以司馬
punctuated: 十二律生而五聲和矣，五聲和，可以被諸八音而爲樂矣。夫如是，則凡八音之器，其輕重、大小、長短、厚薄、多寡、盈縮之數，皆本之律。其體則天地之體，其用之和而能感通天地也，不亦宜哉？粤自黄帝始命伶倫造十二律之管，吹陽律以候於鳳者六，曰黄鍾、太簇、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射是也；吹陰律以候於凰者六，曰大吕、夾鍾、仲吕、林鍾、南吕、應鍾是也。故能協和中聲，候氣不爽，清濁相符，倫理無失。而後世之言律者，實肇於此。唐虞三代，弗可尚已。自是而下，制作紛紛，卒未有歸一之論。以漢言之，相統之法，三五不周；畸羸之數，損益不用。京房之見尚如此，彼張蒼之輩又何足望也？庶幾者，其司馬遷乎！以唐言之，梁陳之音，采而雜用；周齊之技，集而合作。祖孝孫之見尚如此，彼魏延陵之徒又何足道也？庶幾者，其張文收乎！至於有宋之時，雖以司馬
translation_en:
…Once the twelve pitch standards are generated, the five notes become harmonious; when the five notes are harmonious, they can be applied to the eight categories of musical instruments to make music. Thus, for all instruments in these eight categories, the numerical measures governing weight, size, length, thickness, quantity, and expansion or contraction are all grounded in the pitch standards. Their substance is the substance of Heaven and Earth. Is it not fitting, then, that the harmony of their operation can resonate and communicate with Heaven and Earth?

It began when the Yellow Emperor commanded Ling Lun to fashion pipes for the twelve pitch standards. Six yang pitches were sounded and tested against the calls of the male phoenix: Huangzhong, Taicu, Guxian, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi. Six yin pitches were sounded and tested against the calls of the female phoenix: Dalü, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong. Thus they could harmonize correctly tuned sounds, register the vital force without error, bring high and low tones into accord, and preserve their proper order. Later discussions of pitch standards truly originated here. The achievements of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties could not be surpassed. Thereafter, systems and constructions proliferated, but no unified account was ever reached.

To speak of the Han: in the method of mutual coordination [?], the threes and fives failed to complete their cycles; with fractional remainders and surpluses, subtraction and addition could not be applied [?]. If even Jing Fang’s understanding was like this, what could one expect of men such as Zhang Cang? Perhaps Sima Qian came close!

To speak of the Tang: the music of Liang and Chen was selected and used in a mixture, while the techniques of Zhou and Qi were assembled and combined. If even Zu Xiaosun’s understanding was like this, what is there to say of men such as Wei Yanling? Perhaps Zhang Wenshou came close! As for the Song period, even with Sima’s…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
光范鎮之賢猶屑屑於黍尺之際而不知
聲氣之求獨一蔡西山之正顧乃棄而弗
用徒托諸空言而已矣蓋嘗考之聲有五
也必以律而和之假令黃鍾爲宮則太簇
爲商姑洗爲角林鍾爲徵南呂爲羽大呂
爲宮則夾鍾爲商仲呂爲角夷則爲徵無
射爲羽其他律呂亦皆以次而和也氣有
十二也必以律而候之假令冬至則黃鍾
應氣升五分一釐三毫大寒則大呂應氣
===
升三分七釐六毫其他律呂亦皆以時而
候也天地之數十而黃鍾之實九用者約
體之十以爲九使損益無奇零之積乃黃
鍾之用數也黃鍾之數九而黃鍾之長用
十者分用之九以爲十使乘積得九九之
實乃黃鍾之體數也平置十二分均而方
之規而員之有餘不足各四而爲全分者
一規外四餘不用而得方分者九此非嘗
員而分方之說乎仲呂之實以三分之不
punctuated:
光、范鎮之賢，猶屑屑於黍尺之際，而不知聲氣之求。獨一蔡西山之正，顧乃棄而弗用，徒托諸空言而已矣。
蓋嘗考之：聲有五也，必以律而和之。假令黃鍾爲宮，則太簇爲商，姑洗爲角，林鍾爲徵，南呂爲羽；大呂爲宮，則夾鍾爲商，仲呂爲角，夷則爲徵，無射爲羽。其他律呂，亦皆以次而和也。氣有十二也，必以律而候之。假令冬至，則黃鍾應氣，升五分一釐三毫；大寒，則大呂應氣，升三分七釐六毫。其他律呂，亦皆以時而候也。
天地之數十，而黃鍾之實九。用者約體之十以爲九，使損益無奇零之積，乃黃鍾之用數也。黃鍾之數九，而黃鍾之長用十者，分用之九以爲十，使乘積得九九之實，乃黃鍾之體數也。平置十二分，均而方之，規而員之，有餘不足各四，而爲全分者一。規外四餘不用，而得方分者九，此非嘗員而分方之說乎？仲呂之實，以三分之不
translation_en:
…Guang and Fan Zhen, despite their worthiness, still busied themselves with millet grains and measuring rules, without knowing to investigate sound and qi. Only Cai Xishan’s approach was correct; yet it was discarded and left unused, entrusted merely to empty words.
I have examined the matter. There are five notes, which must be harmonized by means of the pitch standards. If Huangzhong serves as gong, then Taicu serves as shang, Guxian as jue, Linzhong as zhi, and Nanlü as yu. If Dalü serves as gong, then Jiazhong serves as shang, Zhonglü as jue, Yize as zhi, and Wuyi as yu. The other pitch standards likewise harmonize in their respective sequences. There are twelve seasonal qi, which must be observed by means of the pitch pipes. At the winter solstice, Huangzhong responds to the qi, which rises five fen, one li, and three hao; at Great Cold, Dalü responds to the qi, which rises three fen, seven li, and six hao. The other pitch pipes likewise serve to observe the qi at their respective times.
The number of Heaven and Earth is ten, while Huangzhong’s numerical value is nine. For calculation, the ten of its substance is reduced to nine, so that subtraction and addition produce no fractional remainders: this is Huangzhong’s functional number. Huangzhong’s number is nine, but ten is used for its length: the nine of its function is divided into ten, so that multiplication yields the value of nine times nine. This is Huangzhong’s substantial number. Lay out twelve equal divisions on a plane, form them into a square, and use a compass to make a circle. There are four portions in excess and four deficient, with one forming a complete division. Discarding the four excess portions outside the circle leaves nine square divisions. Is this not the explanation of making a circle and dividing it into squares [?]? When Zhonglü’s numerical value is divided by three, it does not …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
盡二筭以變律之六而得六三之數因六
三之積而乘仲呂之實此非律正而有變
之說乎子一者黃鍾之律也其寅九則黃
鍾之寸數辰八十一則黃鍾之分數午七
百二十九則黃鍾之釐數申六千五百六
十一則黃鍾之毫數戌五萬九千四十九
則黃鍾之絲數此以一爲一者也亥一十
七萬七千一百四十七者黃鍾之實也其
酉一萬九千六百八十三爲黃鍾之寸法
===
未二千一百八十七爲黃鍾之分法巳二
百四十三爲黃鍾之釐法卯二十七爲黃
鍾之毫法丑三爲黃鍾之絲法此以三爲
一者也午申戌本陰辰而曰陽者豈非以
蕤賓夷則無射三陽律在位耶巳卯丑本
陽辰而曰陰者豈非以林鍾南呂應鍾三
陰律在位耶黃鍾一分爲九寸林鍾得九
之六太蔟得九之八南呂得九之五十分
寸之三姑洗得九之七十分寸之一應鍾
punctuated: 盡二，筭以變律之六而得六三之數，因六三之積而乘仲呂之實，此非律正而有變之說乎？子一者，黃鍾之律也。其寅九則黃鍾之寸數，辰八十一則黃鍾之分數，午七百二十九則黃鍾之釐數，申六千五百六十一則黃鍾之毫數，戌五萬九千四十九則黃鍾之絲數，此以一爲一者也。亥一十七萬七千一百四十七者，黃鍾之實也。其酉一萬九千六百八十三爲黃鍾之寸法，未二千一百八十七爲黃鍾之分法，巳二百四十三爲黃鍾之釐法，卯二十七爲黃鍾之毫法，丑三爲黃鍾之絲法，此以三爲一者也。午申戌本陰辰而曰陽者，豈非以蕤賓、夷則、無射三陽律在位耶？巳卯丑本陽辰而曰陰者，豈非以林鍾、南呂、應鍾三陰律在位耶？黃鍾一分爲九寸，林鍾得九之六，太蔟得九之八，南呂得九之五十分寸之三，姑洗得九之七十分寸之一，應鍾
translation_en:
…leaving a remainder of two. Calculating with the six altered pitch standards yields the number “six-three” [?]; taking this accumulated value and multiplying the numerical magnitude of Zhonglü by it—is this not the explanation of how the pitch standards have both regular and altered forms?

The one associated with zi represents the Huangzhong pitch standard. The nine associated with yin is Huangzhong’s number in cun; the eighty-one associated with chen is its number in fen; the seven hundred twenty-nine associated with wu is its number in li; the six thousand five hundred sixty-one associated with shen is its number in hao; and the fifty-nine thousand forty-nine associated with xu is its number in si. This is the method that takes one as one. The one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven associated with hai is Huangzhong’s numerical magnitude. The nineteen thousand six hundred eighty-three associated with you is its divisor for cun; the two thousand one hundred eighty-seven associated with wei is its divisor for fen; the two hundred forty-three associated with si is its divisor for li; the twenty-seven associated with mao is its divisor for hao; and the three associated with chou is its divisor for si. This is the method that takes three as one.

Wu, shen, and xu are originally yin positions, yet are called yang: is this not because the three yang pitch standards, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi, occupy those positions? Si, mao, and chou are originally yang positions, yet are called yin: is this not because the three yin pitch standards, Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong, occupy those positions?

One unit of Huangzhong is divided into nine cun. Linzhong obtains six of the nine, and Taicu eight of the nine. Nanlü obtains five of the nine plus three tenths of a cun [?]; Guxian obtains seven of the nine plus one tenth of a cun [?]; Yingzhong…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
蕤賓得金鐘大呂長則得金毫大鐘無射
得金簇而仲呂則得九之六有五分八釐
三毫四絲六忽此十一律之生專主黃鍾
而言者也至於黃鍾損一而得林鍾林鍾
益一而得太簇太簇損一而得南呂南呂
益一而得姑洗姑洗損一而得應鍾應鍾
益一而得蕤賓蕤賓損一而得大呂大呂
益一而得夷則夷則損一而得夾鍾夾鍾
益一而得無射無射損一而得仲呂非以
===
十二律互相生而言之者乎黃鍾而大呂
大呂而太簇太簇而夾鍾夾鍾而姑洗姑
洗而仲呂仲呂而蕤賓蕤賓而林鍾林鍾
而夷則夷則而南呂南呂而無射無射而
應鍾此以陰陽長短之序而言之者也至
於黃鍾隔八下生林鍾林鍾隔八上生太
簇太簇隔八下生南呂南呂隔八上生姑
洗姑洗隔八下生應鍾應鍾隔八上生蕤
賓蕤賓隔八下生大呂大呂隔八上生夷
punctuated: 蕤賓得金鐘，大呂長則得金毫大鐘，無射得金簇，而仲呂則得九之六，有五分八釐三毫四絲六忽。此十一律之生，專主黃鍾而言者也。至於黃鍾損一而得林鍾，林鍾益一而得太簇，太簇損一而得南呂，南呂益一而得姑洗，姑洗損一而得應鍾，應鍾益一而得蕤賓，蕤賓損一而得大呂，大呂益一而得夷則，夷則損一而得夾鍾，夾鍾益一而得無射，無射損一而得仲呂，非以十二律互相生而言之者乎？黃鍾而大呂，大呂而太簇，太簇而夾鍾，夾鍾而姑洗，姑洗而仲呂，仲呂而蕤賓，蕤賓而林鍾，林鍾而夷則，夷則而南呂，南呂而無射，無射而應鍾，此以陰陽長短之序而言之者也。至於黃鍾隔八下生林鍾，林鍾隔八上生太簇，太簇隔八下生南呂，南呂隔八上生姑洗，姑洗隔八下生應鍾，應鍾隔八上生蕤賓，蕤賓隔八下生大呂，大呂隔八上生夷
translation_en: … Ruibin yields “jinzhong” [?]; the length of Dalu yields “jinhao dazhong” [?]; Wuyi yields “jincu” [?]; and Zhonglü obtains six of the nine cun, plus five fen, eight li, three hao, four si, and six hu. This account of the generation of the eleven pitch standards takes Huangzhong alone as its basis. As for reducing Huangzhong by one-third to obtain Linzhong, increasing Linzhong by one-third to obtain Taicu, reducing Taicu by one-third to obtain Nanlü, increasing Nanlü by one-third to obtain Guxian, reducing Guxian by one-third to obtain Yingzhong, increasing Yingzhong by one-third to obtain Ruibin, reducing Ruibin by one-third to obtain Dalu, increasing Dalu by one-third to obtain Yize, reducing Yize by one-third to obtain Jiazhong, increasing Jiazhong by one-third to obtain Wuyi, and reducing Wuyi by one-third to obtain Zhonglü—is this not an account of the twelve pitch standards generating one another? Huangzhong is followed by Dalu, Dalu by Taicu, Taicu by Jiazhong, Jiazhong by Guxian, Guxian by Zhonglü, Zhonglü by Ruibin, Ruibin by Linzhong, Linzhong by Yize, Yize by Nanlü, Nanlü by Wuyi, and Wuyi by Yingzhong: this describes their sequence according to yin and yang and the lengths of their pitch pipes. As for Huangzhong generating Linzhong downward at the eighth position, Linzhong generating Taicu upward at the eighth position, Taicu generating Nanlü downward at the eighth position, Nanlü generating Guxian upward at the eighth position, Guxian generating Yingzhong downward at the eighth position, Yingzhong generating Ruibin upward at the eighth position, Ruibin generating Dalu downward at the eighth position, and Dalu generating Yi… upward at the eighth position…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
則夷則隔八下生夾鍾夾鍾隔八上生無
射無射隔八下生仲吕非以十一律相生
之序而言之者乎六十調者十二律盡五
聲五聲各得十二律以律之十二乘聲之
五共六十調所謂乘五而得者如此八十
四聲者十二律盡七聲七聲各得十二律
以律之十二乘聲之七共八十四聲所謂
乘七而得者如此以變律而言之黄鍾爲
君不爲他律役其爲商爲角則受無射夷
===
則之役其爲徵爲羽則受仲吕夾鍾之役
黄鍾既變而餘律從之黄鍾林鍾太簇南
吕姑洗應鍾爲上六律以上而役下通而
和蕤賔大吕夷則夾鍾無射仲吕爲下六
律以下而役上乖而戾必少下上律之聲
以和下律之音由此觀之則二說之皆是
可知矣以飛灰言之自冬至而夏至氣升
而灰可飛自小暑而大雪氣降而灰不可
飛是亦疑若似矣殊不知陰陽升降有一
punctuated: 則，夷則隔八下生夾鍾，夾鍾隔八上生無射，無射隔八下生仲吕，非以十一律相生之序而言之者乎？六十調者，十二律盡五聲，五聲各得十二律，以律之十二乘聲之五，共六十調，所謂乘五而得者如此。八十四聲者，十二律盡七聲，七聲各得十二律，以律之十二乘聲之七，共八十四聲，所謂乘七而得者如此。以變律而言之，黄鍾爲君，不爲他律役；其爲商爲角，則受無射、夷則之役；其爲徵爲羽，則受仲吕、夾鍾之役。黄鍾既變，而餘律從之。黄鍾、林鍾、太簇、南吕、姑洗、應鍾爲上六律，以上而役下，通而和；蕤賔、大吕、夷則、夾鍾、無射、仲吕爲下六律，以下而役上，乖而戾。必少下上律之聲，以和下律之音。由此觀之，則二說之皆是可知矣。以飛灰言之，自冬至而夏至，氣升而灰可飛；自小暑而大雪，氣降而灰不可飛，是亦疑若似矣。殊不知陰陽升降有一
translation_en:
…[Yi]ze; Yize generates Jiazhong downward at an interval of eight, Jiazhong generates Wuyi upward at an interval of eight, and Wuyi generates Zhonglü downward at an interval of eight. Is this not speaking of the sequence in which the eleven pitch standards generate one another? As for the sixty modes, the twelve pitch standards encompass all five notes, and each of the five notes receives all twelve pitch standards. Multiplying the twelve pitch standards by the five notes yields sixty modes in total. This is what is meant by obtaining them through multiplication by five. As for the eighty-four tones, the twelve pitch standards encompass all seven notes, and each of the seven notes receives all twelve pitch standards. Multiplying the twelve pitch standards by the seven notes yields eighty-four tones in total. This is what is meant by obtaining them through multiplication by seven.

Speaking of altered pitch standards, Huangzhong acts as ruler and does not serve any other pitch standard. When it acts as shang or jue, however, it serves Wuyi or Yize respectively; when it acts as zhi or yu, it serves Zhonglü or Jiazhong respectively. Once Huangzhong is altered, the other pitch standards follow it. Huangzhong, Linzhong, Taicu, Nanlü, Guxian, and Yingzhong constitute the upper six pitch standards. When the upper standards command the lower, the relationship is smooth and harmonious. Ruibin, Dalü, Yize, Jiazhong, Wuyi, and Zhonglü constitute the lower six pitch standards. When the lower standards command the upper, the relationship is discordant and contrary. One must slightly lower the tones of the upper pitch standards to harmonize them with those of the lower pitch standards. Viewed in this light, both explanations can be understood to be correct.

Speaking of flying ashes, from the Winter Solstice to the Summer Solstice, qi rises and the ashes can fly; from Minor Heat to Major Snow, qi descends and the ashes cannot fly. This, too, might seem plausible. Yet it fails entirely to recognize that in the rising and falling of yin and yang there is a…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
歲之運自冬至至大雪是巳有一日之□
自子至亥是巳夏至以後固氣降而巳辰
以前則氣升安得不飛灰應候也由此觀
之則二說之是非可見矣嗚呼樂者所以
象功而昭德也堯欽明而時雍則奏大章
舜重華而風動則作大韶苟徒極聲容之
盛而無和樂之實則樂云樂云鍾鼓云乎
哉亦聖人所不取也我
列聖相承禮法制而教化脩三綱正而九疇叙
百姓太和萬物咸若八風之氣宣而天下
之情平矣猗歟盛哉
===
第三問
陸光祖
同考試官訓導鄧 批〔取士之法及士之自立者是如此〕
同考試官訓導塗 批〔豐縟有餘味不止答問目而巳〕
考試官教諭劉 批〔如此策顧不當錄耶〕
考試官學正方 批〔齊整〕
君子之建功也必本於道入主之用□□
punctuated:
歲之運，自冬至至大雪是巳；有一日之□，自子至亥是巳。夏至以後固氣降，而巳辰以前則氣升，安得不飛灰應候也？由此觀之，則二說之是非可見矣。嗚呼！樂者，所以象功而昭德也。堯欽明而時雍，則奏《大章》；舜重華而風動，則作《大韶》。苟徒極聲容之盛，而無和樂之實，則「樂云樂云，鍾鼓云乎哉？」亦聖人所不取也。我列聖相承，禮法制而教化脩，三綱正而九疇叙，百姓太和，萬物咸若，八風之氣宣，而天下之情平矣。猗歟，盛哉！

第三問
陸光祖
同考試官訓導鄧批〔取士之法及士之自立者是如此〕
同考試官訓導塗批〔豐縟有餘味不止答問目而巳〕
考試官教諭劉批〔如此策顧不當錄耶〕
考試官學正方批〔齊整〕

君子之建功也，必本於道；入主之用□□
translation_en:
…the yearly cycle, extending from the winter solstice to Great Snow, is one such instance; there is also the daily □, extending from the zi hour to the hai hour. After the summer solstice, the qi does indeed descend; yet before the si and chen hours [?], it ascends. How, then, could the ashes fail to fly in response to the seasonal indications? Viewed in this light, the correctness or error of the two explanations becomes apparent.

Alas! Music serves to represent achievements and manifest virtue. When Yao was reverent and enlightened and the people lived in harmony, Great Splendor was performed. When Shun renewed the brilliance of his predecessor and his influence spread like the wind, Great Shao was composed. If one merely brings sound and ceremonial display to their utmost magnificence, without the substance of harmony and joy, then: “Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?” This, too, is something the sage would reject. Our successive sage emperors have inherited the throne in turn. Ritual and law have been established, moral instruction cultivated, the Three Bonds rectified, and the Nine Categories set in order. The common people enjoy profound harmony, and all things follow their proper course. The qi of the eight winds circulates freely, and the feelings of all under Heaven are at peace. Ah, how splendid!

Third Question
Lu Guangzu
