Associate Examiner Tu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Rich and elaborate, with a lingering savor; it does more than merely answer the points in the question.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Should a policy essay like this not indeed be included in the record?〕
Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: 〔Orderly and well arranged.〕

When a gentleman establishes achievements, he must take the Way as his foundation; in the ruler’s employment of □□ [?]…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
不拘其迹夫天下之事未嘗不以得人而
興不得人而廢天下之士未嘗不以知道
爲賢不知道爲不肖然士之於道也有淺
深而見於功業有大小彼顓顓焉不知道
爲何物者適足以敗天下之事以自僨而
已矣人主者操天下之衡以軆天下之士
亦惟舉其賢而進之取其不肖者而退之
使進之而拘其迹則進賢之路不廣退之
而拘其迹則退不肖之法不嚴路不廣則
===
君子或滯於不用法不嚴則小人或幸於
苟容是故少而賢也吾進之少而不肖也
吾退之老而賢也吾進之老而不肖也吾
退之吾有道而已矣年之老少吾何計哉
古者登崇俊良與之共政摧折鎮定付之
以爪牙之寄咨議論思委之以腹心之寄
雖以武王之聖穆公之賢漢唐而下諸君
之英武亦必資於太公蹇叔之流或有以
興創業中興之烈或有以成治內捍外之
punctuated: 不拘其迹。夫天下之事，未嘗不以得人而興，不得人而廢。天下之士，未嘗不以知道爲賢，不知道爲不肖。然士之於道也有淺深，而見於功業有大小。彼顓顓焉不知道爲何物者，適足以敗天下之事，以自僨而已矣。人主者，操天下之衡，以軆天下之士，亦惟舉其賢而進之，取其不肖者而退之。使進之而拘其迹，則進賢之路不廣；退之而拘其迹，則退不肖之法不嚴。路不廣，則君子或滯於不用；法不嚴，則小人或幸於苟容。是故少而賢也，吾進之；少而不肖也，吾退之；老而賢也，吾進之；老而不肖也，吾退之。吾有道而已矣，年之老少，吾何計哉？古者登崇俊良，與之共政；摧折鎮定，付之以爪牙之寄；咨議論思，委之以腹心之寄。雖以武王之聖、穆公之賢、漢唐而下諸君之英武，亦必資於太公、蹇叔之流，或有以興創業中興之烈，或有以成治內捍外之
translation_en:
…without being constrained by their outward circumstances. The affairs of the realm have always flourished through obtaining the right men and fallen into ruin through failing to obtain them. Scholars of the realm have always been deemed worthy for understanding the Way, and unworthy for failing to understand it. Yet scholars understand the Way to differing depths, and their achievements accordingly differ in magnitude. Those narrow-minded men who do not know what the Way is can only ruin the affairs of the realm and bring about their own downfall. The ruler holds the scales of the realm with which to assess [?] its scholars: he need only select the worthy and advance them, and identify the unworthy and dismiss them. If, in advancing men, he is constrained by their outward circumstances, the path for advancing the worthy will not be broad; if, in dismissing men, he is constrained by their outward circumstances, the rules for dismissing the unworthy will not be strict. If the path is not broad, gentlemen may languish without employment; if the rules are not strict, petty men may luckily find themselves improperly tolerated. Thus, if a man is young and worthy, I advance him; if young and unworthy, I dismiss him. If a man is old and worthy, I advance him; if old and unworthy, I dismiss him. I have only the Way as my standard. Why should I reckon whether a man is old or young?

In antiquity, rulers promoted and honored the outstanding and good, sharing government with them. Those who could crush opposition and restore stability were entrusted with responsibility as the ruler’s claws and teeth; those who could offer counsel, deliberate, and reflect were entrusted with responsibility as his heart and belly. Even with the sageliness of King Wu, the worthiness of Duke Mu, and the martial prowess of the rulers from the Han and Tang onward, they still had to rely upon men such as Taigong and Jian Shu. Some thereby accomplished the great deeds of founding a dynasty or restoring its fortunes; others thereby achieved success in governing within and defending against threats from without …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
功當是時也擇賢而用之隨才而使之初
何嘗論其年之老少乎且新法之行舉天
下稱其不便而始終附會之者曾布也入
將曰年少者之所爲也是豈年少之病哉
人自病耳今以一人而盡疑天下之年少
者不猶因噎以廢食者乎天書之誤舉朝
廷知其不可而一言賛成之者杜鎬也人
將曰年邁者之所爲也是豈年邁之病哉
人自病耳今以一人而盡疑天下之年邁
===
者不猶因刖而廢屨者乎以年少者而言
之孝平不造西漢之鼎已移於巨君之手
矣鄧仲華杖策以從光武數言之間而天
下之大計以定其爲雲臺之冠不亦宜哉
獻生不辰東漢之鹿已su於孟德之手矣
周公瑾決策以賛孫權一炬之火而江東
之大勢以張其成赤壁之功不亦奇哉老
瞞之下江陵也戰檄一示而羣臣失色張
昭輩已倡迎降之議合孫吴之勢而却之
punctuated:
功。當是時也，擇賢而用之，隨才而使之，初何嘗論其年之老少乎？且新法之行，舉天下稱其不便，而始終附會之者，曾布也。入將曰：「年少者之所爲也。」是豈年少之病哉？人自病耳。今以一人而盡疑天下之年少者，不猶因噎以廢食者乎？天書之誤，舉朝廷知其不可，而一言賛成之者，杜鎬也。人將曰：「年邁者之所爲也。」是豈年邁之病哉？人自病耳。今以一人而盡疑天下之年邁者，不猶因刖而廢屨者乎？

以年少者而言之，孝平不造，西漢之鼎已移於巨君之手矣。鄧仲華杖策以從光武，數言之間，而天下之大計以定，其爲雲臺之冠，不亦宜哉？獻生不辰，東漢之鹿已su於孟德之手矣。周公瑾決策以賛孫權，一炬之火，而江東之大勢以張，其成赤壁之功，不亦奇哉？老瞞之下江陵也，戰檄一示，而羣臣失色。張昭輩已倡迎降之議，合孫吴之勢而却之
translation_en:
…achievements. At that time, they selected worthy men for employment and assigned them duties according to their abilities. When did they ever consider whether these men were old or young? Moreover, when the New Policies were implemented, all under Heaven declared them harmful, yet Zeng Bu supported them from beginning to end. People [?] will say, “This was the doing of a young man.” But how could this be a fault of youth? The fault lay with the man himself. To distrust all young men under Heaven now because of one individual—is this not like giving up eating for fear of choking? As for the error of the heavenly writings, the entire court knew it was unacceptable, yet Du Hao endorsed it with a single utterance. People will say, “This was the doing of an elderly man.” But how could this be a fault of old age? The fault lay with the man himself. To distrust all elderly men under Heaven now because of one individual—is this not like abandoning shoes because someone has had his feet amputated?

To speak of young men: Emperor Xiaoping met with misfortune, and the tripods of Western Han sovereignty had already passed into the hands of Jujun [Wang Mang]. Deng Zhonghua [Deng Yu] took up his staff and followed Guangwu; in the space of a few remarks, the grand strategy for the realm was settled. Was it not fitting that he should rank foremost among the men commemorated in the Cloud Terrace? Emperor Xian was born into ill-starred times, and the deer of Eastern Han sovereignty had already fallen [?] into the hands of Mengde [Cao Cao]. Zhou Gongjin [Zhou Yu] settled the strategy in support of Sun Quan; with the fire of a single torch, Jiangdong’s strategic power expanded. Was not his achievement at Chibi extraordinary? When Old Man [Cao Cao] descended upon Jiangling, the mere presentation of his war proclamation made all the ministers turn pale. Zhang Zhao and his associates had already advocated receiving him and surrendering; the man who united the strength of Sun Wu and repelled him…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
者亢之所以爲人龍也契丹之寇澶淵也
邊書一告而中外震駭欽若輩已建出狩
之策得高瓊之助而退之者準之所以爲
鎻鑰也種溫既入關中王景畧留心江左
捫虱而談當世之務可謂三秦豪傑之才
矣惜溫之不見知金虜既陷中原岳鵬舉
𢿱手雲燕建節而負滅金之志可謂南渡
精忠之將矣惜檜之不見容溫造爲御史
而劾李祐祐爲之膽落其風力可嘉也韓
===
琦任招討而鎮西夏賊爲之膽寒其威名
可畏也數君子者皆年少之人也而建立
乃如此豈奸諛皆如布者哉以年邁者而
言之周武怒商受之虐爲伐商之舉得太
公以爲輔卒成四海永清之功牧野洋洋
之頌至今尚昭昭也秦穆信杞子之言爲
侵鄭之謀忽蹇叔而不聽卒獲三帥被囚
之恥良士番番之戒至今尚耿耿也趙充
國以萬三百餘人而屯田其智將之流矣
punctuated: 者，亢之所以爲人龍也。契丹之寇澶淵也，邊書一告，而中外震駭。欽若輩已建出狩之策，得高瓊之助而退之者，準之所以爲鎻鑰也。種溫既入關中，王景畧留心江左，捫虱而談當世之務，可謂三秦豪傑之才矣，惜溫之不見知。金虜既陷中原，岳鵬舉𢿱手雲燕，建節而負滅金之志，可謂南渡精忠之將矣，惜檜之不見容。溫造爲御史而劾李祐，祐爲之膽落，其風力可嘉也。韓琦任招討而鎮西夏，賊爲之膽寒，其威名可畏也。數君子者，皆年少之人也，而建立乃如此，豈奸諛皆如布者哉？以年邁者而言之，周武怒商受之虐，爲伐商之舉，得太公以爲輔，卒成四海永清之功，《牧野洋洋》之頌，至今尚昭昭也。秦穆信杞子之言，爲侵鄭之謀，忽蹇叔而不聽，卒獲三帥被囚之恥，良士番番之戒，至今尚耿耿也。趙充國以萬三百餘人而屯田，其智將之流矣。
translation_en:
…it was by doing this that Kang [?] proved himself a dragon among men. When the Khitan invaded Chanyuan, a single report from the frontier shook court and country alike. Qinruo and his associates had already proposed that the emperor leave on an imperial tour; it was by obtaining Gao Qiong’s assistance and repelling the enemy that Zhun proved himself the realm’s lock and key. After Zhong Wen [?; apparently Huan Wen] entered Guanzhong, Wang Jinglüe set his mind on Jiangzuo. Picking lice as he discussed the affairs of the age, he could indeed be called an outstanding talent of the Three Qin region. Alas, Wen failed to appreciate him. After the Jin invaders overran the Central Plain, Yue Pengju extended his reach toward Yun and Yan [?]. Bearing the commander’s tally and cherishing the ambition to destroy the Jin, he could indeed be called a general of pure loyalty in the era of the southward retreat. Alas, Hui would not tolerate him. Serving as a censor, Wen Zao impeached Li You, causing You to lose his nerve: his forceful integrity deserves praise. Serving as a Military Commissioner, Han Qi held the Western Xia in check, causing the rebels to tremble: his formidable reputation inspired awe.

These gentlemen were all young men, yet their achievements were such as these. Could they all have been treacherous flatterers like Bu? To speak of elderly men, King Wu of Zhou, angered by the cruelty of Shou of Shang, undertook a campaign against Shang. Securing the assistance of the Grand Duke, he ultimately achieved enduring peace throughout the Four Seas. The eulogy declaring “Vast are the plains of Mu” remains illustrious to this day. Duke Mu of Qin believed Qi Zi’s words and planned an invasion of Zheng. He disregarded Jian Shu and would not listen, ultimately suffering the disgrace of having his three commanders taken prisoner. The admonition concerning “worthy men, advanced in years” remains vivid to this day. Zhao Chongguo established military agricultural colonies with over ten thousand three hundred men; he belonged to the ranks of wise generals.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
當是時先零倡亂於先罪开脅從於後漢
之邊鄙蓋擾擾也卒之罪开既服而先零
亦降充國之功不亦多乎燭之武以十數
言而存鄭其辯士之流矣當是時晉軍於
函陵秦軍於氾南鄭之社稷蓋岌岌也卒
之秦伯既悅而晉侯亦解之武之功不亦
茂乎天后革唐之號自立爲帝罪莫大焉
廷誅倖幸而復唐於周者張柬之也陽城
論列延齡營救陸贄罪莫測焉廷拜言官
===
而名重天下者張萬福也馬援以矍鑠示
勇而天子稱嘆其心可謂壯矣文彥慱以
相業顯名而虜使動容其儀可以象矣數
君子者皆年邁之人也而勲名乃如此豈
昏庸皆若鎬者哉爲今之計者少不必拘
也少而如布之姦諛則斥之如孔明諸人
則用之老不必拘也老而如鎬之昏庸則
去之如太公諸人則進之進而用之者皆
賢也斥而去之者皆不肖也年之老少吾
punctuated:
當是時，先零倡亂於先，罪开脅從於後，漢之邊鄙蓋擾擾也。卒之，罪开既服，而先零亦降，充國之功不亦多乎？燭之武以十數言而存鄭，其辯士之流矣。當是時，晉軍於函陵，秦軍於氾南，鄭之社稷蓋岌岌也。卒之，秦伯既悅，而晉侯亦解，之武之功不亦茂乎？天后革唐之號，自立爲帝，罪莫大焉。廷誅倖幸而復唐於周者，張柬之也。陽城論列延齡，營救陸贄，罪莫測焉。廷拜言官而名重天下者，張萬福也。馬援以矍鑠示勇，而天子稱嘆，其心可謂壯矣。文彥慱以相業顯名，而虜使動容，其儀可以象矣。數君子者，皆年邁之人也，而勲名乃如此，豈昏庸皆若鎬者哉？
爲今之計者，少不必拘也。少而如布之姦諛，則斥之；如孔明諸人，則用之。老不必拘也。老而如鎬之昏庸，則去之；如太公諸人，則進之。進而用之者，皆賢也；斥而去之者，皆不肖也。年之老少，吾
translation_en:
At that time, the Xianling first instigated rebellion, and the Zui-Kai [?] subsequently followed under duress; the Han frontier was in turmoil. In the end, the Zui-Kai [?] submitted, and the Xianling also surrendered. Were Chongguo’s achievements not considerable? With a mere dozen or so words, Zhu Zhiwu preserved Zheng: he belonged among the skilled persuaders. At that time, Jin’s army was encamped at Hanling and Qin’s at Fannan; the state of Zheng was in grave peril. In the end, the Earl of Qin was won over, and the Marquis of Jin also withdrew. Were Zhiwu’s achievements not splendid? The Heavenly Empress changed the dynastic name of Tang and established herself as emperor: no crime could have been greater. It was Zhang Jianzhi who executed the court favorites [?] at court and restored Tang in place of Zhou. Yang Cheng denounced Yanling and sought to rescue Lu Zhi, facing punishment whose severity could not be foreseen. It was Zhang Wanfu who bowed to the remonstrance officials at court and thereby won renown throughout the realm. Ma Yuan displayed his vigor to demonstrate his courage, and the Son of Heaven praised him: his spirit could indeed be called stalwart. Wen Yanbo [?] won distinction through his achievements as chief councilor, and even the foreign envoy was visibly moved: his deportment could serve as a model. These gentlemen were all advanced in years, yet such were their achievements and reputations. Could all elderly men be as muddleheaded and inept as Gao?
In deciding what to do today, youth need not be a restriction. If a young man is as treacherous and sycophantic as Bu, reject him; if he resembles Kongming and the others, employ him. Old age need not be a restriction either. If an old man is as muddleheaded and inept as Gao, dismiss him; if he resembles Taigong and the others, advance him. Those advanced and employed will all be worthy; those rejected and dismissed will all be unworthy. As for whether they are old or young, I …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
不得而知之也嗟夫天下之事功未有不
本於道者也事功而不本於道是功利私
智而已然求人才於三代之上道純而功
亦隆求人才於三代之下則亦隨其分之
所得而爲功之所著耳太公不可尚矣孔
明可興禮樂蓋天民之未粹者其餘諸君
子或得其一偏而全體之未虧或資之暗
合而造詣之未盡故亦能因事而有成隨
試而輙效也其下如布如鎬者得免於王
誅亦幸矣何道之足云哉
===
第四問
同考試官教諭王　批〔脩復〕
劉懷仁
祖宗之法馬政自舉確論也
考試官教諭劉　批〔縱横馳騁不拘問目當是策手〕
考試官學正方　批
祖宗之法爲必可守有識之士也
經天下之政存乎法行天下之法存乎人
punctuated:
不得而知之也。嗟夫！天下之事功，未有不本於道者也。事功而不本於道，是功利私智而已。然求人才於三代之上，道純而功亦隆；求人才於三代之下，則亦隨其分之所得，而爲功之所著耳。太公不可尚矣，孔明可興禮樂，蓋天民之未粹者。其餘諸君子，或得其一偏而全體之未虧，或資之暗合而造詣之未盡，故亦能因事而有成，隨試而輙效也。其下如布如鎬者，得免於王誅亦幸矣，何道之足云哉！

第四問
同考試官教諭王，批〔脩復〕
劉懷仁
祖宗之法，馬政自舉，確論也。
考試官教諭劉，批〔縱横馳騁，不拘問目，當是策手〕
考試官學正方，批：
祖宗之法爲必可守，有識之士也。

經天下之政存乎法，行天下之法存乎人。
translation_en:
…I need not know their age. Alas! No achievement in the affairs of the world has ever failed to rest upon the Way. Achievements that do not rest upon the Way amount merely to the pursuit of profit and the exercise of private cleverness. Yet if we seek talented men in the Three Dynasties and earlier, their Way was pure and their achievements likewise great. If we seek talented men after the Three Dynasties, their achievements were manifest only in accordance with the measure of the Way each had attained. Taigong cannot be surpassed. Kongming could have revived rites and music; he was perhaps one of Heaven’s people, though not yet wholly pure. Of the other gentlemen, some grasped one aspect without impairing the whole; others were endowed with qualities that accorded implicitly with the Way, though their attainments were incomplete. Thus they too could achieve success as circumstances arose and prove effective whenever put to the test. As for those below them, such as Bu and Gao, they were fortunate even to escape royal execution. What understanding of the Way could they claim?

Fourth Question
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔Restore and repair [?].〕
Liu Huairen
“With the laws of the ancestors, horse administration will naturally be put into effect: this is a sound argument.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔“He ranges freely, unconstrained by the particulars of the question. He must be an accomplished writer of policy essays.”〕
Examiner Fang, Instructor (xuezheng), comments:
“He holds that the laws of the ancestors can assuredly be upheld: a man of discernment.”

Ordering the governance of the realm depends upon laws; putting the laws of the realm into practice depends upon people.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
故爲治者不患法之不脩而患人之未得
吾見法具而不得其人者有矣未見得其
人而法有不舉者也馬政之制
國朝之經畫已備特承平日久怠於吏而玩
於民法固未嘗有敝也敝之者人也今能
一振而作之其所以經天下者沛乎有餘
裕焉苟徒是古非今役役於紛更改革之
勞而不知脩復之道其爲爲治之累豈小
小哉孔子曰文武之政布在方策其人存
===
則其政舉其人亡則其政息不我欺也請
因明問而復之武王之伐商也有駟騵彭
彭之詩魯侯之征淮夷也有涇舍牛馬之
誓則馬之用於征伐也尚矣玁狁整居焦
穫矣而宣王成薄伐之功者以騏翼鑾鑣
之盛高帝威加海内矣而匈奴肆平城之
圍者以龍驪駮白之多則馬之係於成敗
也大矣此歷代以來所以考成分屬有番
育之官祈休報賜有歲時之祭也以其官
punctuated: 故爲治者，不患法之不脩，而患人之未得。吾見法具而不得其人者有矣，未見得其人而法有不舉者也。馬政之制，國朝之經畫已備，特承平日久，怠於吏而玩於民。法固未嘗有敝也，敝之者人也。今能一振而作之，其所以經天下者，沛乎有餘裕焉。苟徒是古非今，役役於紛更改革之勞，而不知脩復之道，其爲爲治之累，豈小小哉！孔子曰：「文武之政，布在方策。其人存，則其政舉；其人亡，則其政息。」不我欺也！請因明問而復之。武王之伐商也，有「駟騵彭彭」之詩；魯侯之征淮夷也，有「涇舍牛馬」之誓。則馬之用於征伐也尚矣。玁狁整居焦穫矣，而宣王成薄伐之功者，以騏翼鑾鑣之盛；高帝威加海内矣，而匈奴肆平城之圍者，以龍驪駮白之多。則馬之係於成敗也大矣。此歷代以來所以考成分屬，有番育之官；祈休報賜，有歲時之祭也。以其官
translation_en:
Thus, those who govern need not worry that the laws have not been put in order, but that the right people have not been found. I have seen cases in which the laws were complete yet the right people were lacking; I have never seen a case in which the right people were obtained yet the laws went unenforced. As for horse administration, the arrangements of our dynasty are already comprehensive. It is merely that, after a long period of peace, officials have grown negligent and the people have treated them lightly. The laws themselves have never been defective; it is people who have impaired them. If we can now make a concerted effort to revive them, they will provide ample means for governing the realm. If, however, we merely approve the past and condemn the present, toiling incessantly at alterations and reforms without understanding how to restore existing institutions, could the resulting burden on government be slight? Confucius said: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set down on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. When the right people are present, that government is carried out; when those people are gone, that government ceases.” These words do not deceive us!
Allow me to respond to your discerning question. When King Wu attacked Shang, there was the verse, “Teams of four white-bellied chestnut horses, mighty and strong.” When the Marquis of Lu campaigned against the Huai Yi, there was the oath concerning “jing she cattle and horses” [?]. Thus, the use of horses in military campaigns is of great antiquity. The Xianyun occupied Jiaohuo in orderly ranks, yet King Xuan succeeded in his punitive campaign through the abundance of his fine horses [?], harness bells, and bridles. Emperor Gao’s might extended throughout the land, yet the Xiongnu boldly besieged him at Pingcheng through the multitude of their “dragon,” black, dappled, and white horses [?]. Thus, horses have a great bearing on success and failure. This is why successive dynasties have assessed results and apportioned responsibilities, establishing officials for breeding and rearing horses; and why they have held seasonal sacrifices to pray for blessings and give thanks for favors bestowed. As for those officials …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
而言之其廄有未央承華騊駼騎馬駱駘
大廄之異其官有三令四令丞五監長之
殊而掌之於太僕者漢制也其署有六閑
八坊四十八監之類其官有主簿直司圉
官牧尉排馬羣頭之屬而領之於大僕者
唐制也至於騏驥有院天駟有監天廄有
坊既置羣牧司又置羣牧使此在內監牧
之法自河北至許州已有十八監兩河陜
西有都總管處復置一監太原交城又復
===
置馬監既委羣牧司又委守倅兼領此在
外監牧之法又非有宋之制乎以其祭而
言之春祭馬祖夏則祭先牧秋祭馬社冬
則祭馬步者周禮也牲用少牢地用大澤
四祭之禮同積柴以燔坎地以埋四神之
禮異者隋禮也至於筮日致齋於未祭之
先瘞埳燎柴於既祭之後又非開元禮乎
肆惟我
國家
punctuated:
而言之，其廄有未央、承華、騊駼、騎馬、駱駘、大廄之異，其官有三令、四令丞、五監長之殊，而掌之於太僕者，漢制也。其署有六閑、八坊、四十八監之類，其官有主簿、直司、圉官、牧尉、排馬、羣頭之屬，而領之於大僕者，唐制也。至於騏驥有院，天駟有監，天廄有坊，既置羣牧司，又置羣牧使，此在內監牧之法。自河北至許州，已有十八監，兩河、陜西有都總管處，復置一監，太原、交城又復置馬監，既委羣牧司，又委守倅兼領，此在外監牧之法，又非有宋之制乎？
以其祭而言之，春祭馬祖，夏則祭先牧，秋祭馬社，冬則祭馬步者，《周禮》也。牲用少牢，地用大澤，四祭之禮同；積柴以燔，坎地以埋，四神之禮異者，隋禮也。至於筮日致齋於未祭之先，瘞埳燎柴於既祭之後，又非《開元禮》乎？肆惟我國家
translation_en:
…speaking of their administration, the stables were distinguished as Weiyang, Chenghua, Taotu, Qima, Luotai, and the Grand Stable. Their officials were differentiated into three directors, four directors and assistants, and five supervisory heads [?], all under the administration of the Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud: this was the Han system. Their establishments included six stables, eight horse farms, and forty-eight directorates; their officials included registrars, duty officers, stable officers, pasture commandants, horse arrangers, and herd heads, all under the Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud: this was the Tang system. As for the Song, there was an office for fine steeds, a directorate for the imperial horses, and a horse farm for the imperial stables. Both a Herds Office and commissioners for the herds were established: these were the arrangements for supervising horse breeding within the capital. From Hebei to Xuzhou there were already eighteen directorates. Wherever there was a commander-in-chief in the Two He regions and Shaanxi, another directorate was established; horse directorates were also established at Taiyuan and Jiaocheng. Responsibility was entrusted both to the Herds Office and concurrently to prefects and their deputies: these were the arrangements for supervising horse breeding outside the capital. Were these not also institutions of the Song dynasty?
Speaking of their sacrifices, sacrificing to the Ancestor of Horses in spring, the First Herdsman in summer, the Patron of Horse Pastures in autumn, and the Horse Stride deity in winter is prescribed in the Rites of Zhou. Using a sheep and a pig as sacrificial victims and a great marsh as the site, with the same ceremonial forms for all four sacrifices, but differing in the rites for the four spirits—piling up firewood for burning or digging a pit for burial—was the ritual practice of the Sui. As for determining the day by milfoil divination and observing ritual purification before the sacrifice, then burying the offerings in a pit or burning them on a woodpile afterward, was this not prescribed in the Rituals of the Kaiyuan Era? Thus, considering our dynasty…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承立經陳紀參之於往昔之規斷之以
聰明之獨其設官不爲不備矣其立法不
爲不詳矣是宜馬之蕃盛也邇者青蜀之
賊一興邊關之冦少警而旣竭之馬則玄
黃
朝廷遣市馬之使帑藏出市馬之錢遂使閭
閻之下櫪爲之一空價值爲之騰湧此
無他良以我
國家長治久安百五十餘年以來天下雍容
===
於禮樂文章之化熙皡於富壽安樂之天
官雖備也世平則易玩法雖詳也歲久則
易湮其欲在內者有有黃有驪之多在外
者有旣佶且閑之盛不亦難哉策曰準今
者必酌乎古將酌古法而行之歟抑我
國家法已詳備今莫若脩其廢墮歟嗟夫泥
古者不通遵先王者無過今舉古人一二
事而言之勸民養馬有一匹者復卒三人
蓋居閑則免三人之筭有事則當三人之
punctuated:
列聖相承，立經陳紀，參之於往昔之規，斷之以聰明之獨。其設官不爲不備矣，其立法不爲不詳矣，是宜馬之蕃盛也。邇者青蜀之賊一興，邊關之冦少警，而旣竭之馬則玄黃。朝廷遣市馬之使，帑藏出市馬之錢，遂使閭閻之下，櫪爲之一空，價值爲之騰湧。此無他，良以我國家長治久安百五十餘年以來，天下雍容於禮樂文章之化，熙皡於富壽安樂之天。官雖備也，世平則易玩；法雖詳也，歲久則易湮。其欲在內者有「有黃有驪」之多，在外者有「旣佶且閑」之盛，不亦難哉？

策曰：「準今者必酌乎古。」將酌古法而行之歟？抑我國家法已詳備，今莫若脩其廢墮歟？嗟夫！泥古者不通，遵先王者無過。今舉古人一二事而言之：勸民養馬，有一匹者復卒三人。蓋居閑則免三人之筭，有事則當三人之
translation_en:
…successive sage emperors have established enduring principles and set forth regulations, consulting the precedents of earlier ages and deciding through their own discerning judgment. Their provision of officials has certainly been comprehensive, and their establishment of laws certainly detailed. Horses ought therefore to have flourished in abundance. Yet recently, as soon as rebels arose in Qing and Shu and raiders caused even a slight alarm at the frontier passes, the already depleted horses were utterly exhausted. The court dispatched envoys to purchase horses, and the treasury disbursed money for their purchase. Consequently, the stables among the common people were emptied, and prices soared. There is no other reason for this than that, during our dynasty’s more than 150 years of lasting order and peace, all under Heaven have lived at ease under the civilizing influence of rites, music, and literary culture, enjoying a flourishing age of wealth, longevity, peace, and happiness. Though the complement of officials is full, peaceful times readily breed negligence; though the laws are detailed, the passage of years readily consigns them to oblivion. Is it not difficult, then, to hope for abundant horses in the interior, “both yellow and black,” and thriving herds beyond it, “both sturdy and well trained”?

The policy question states: “Those who establish standards for the present must weigh the practices of antiquity.” Should we weigh ancient methods and put them into practice? Or, since our dynasty’s laws are already detailed and comprehensive, would it be best now to restore those that have fallen into disuse? Alas! Those who cling rigidly to antiquity lack understanding, but those who follow the former kings do no wrong. Let me now discuss one or two practices of the ancients. To encourage the people to raise horses, anyone possessing one horse was granted exemption from military service for three men. In ordinary times, this meant exemption from the poll taxes of three men; when military needs arose, it counted in place of three men’s …

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
卒此內郡然也縱民畜牧官不爲禁或致
馬千匹或致馬數千此邊塞然也是非漢
制乎當給馬者官與其直市之匹錢二
萬五千刺史折衝果毅歲周察不任戰者
鬻之以其錢更市不足則府供之此給錢
以市也府兵漸壞兵貧難致乃給以監牧
之馬此給馬以用也是非唐制乎至於有
宋之時有曰官馬畜於監牧者也曰民馬
散於編戶者也曰戎馬市於邊郡者也此
===
皆古人之法執事所欲參酌以行之者而
愚生直以爲不可也是何也蓋彼法之善
者當今旣亦采而用之矣其不宜於時者
則又不可行也載考當時之制內有太僕
寺矣而府州縣設佐吏以專領之外有行
太僕矣而苑馬寺設監苑以分領之互市
有茶馬也分蕃有圉長也其設官也擬之
漢唐宋豈不爲尤密乎今亦取其賢者而
任之取其不肖者而退之耳旣有見馬以
punctuated: 卒，此內郡然也。縱民畜牧，官不爲禁，或致馬千匹，或致馬數千，此邊塞然也。是非漢制乎？當給馬者，官與其直市之，匹錢二萬五千。刺史、折衝、果毅歲周察，不任戰者鬻之，以其錢更市，不足則府供之，此給錢以市也。府兵漸壞，兵貧難致，乃給以監牧之馬，此給馬以用也。是非唐制乎？至於有宋之時，有曰官馬，畜於監牧者也；曰民馬，散於編戶者也；曰戎馬，市於邊郡者也。此皆古人之法，執事所欲參酌以行之者，而愚生直以爲不可也。是何也？蓋彼法之善者，當今旣亦采而用之矣；其不宜於時者，則又不可行也。載考當時之制，內有太僕寺矣，而府州縣設佐吏以專領之；外有行太僕矣，而苑馬寺設監苑以分領之。互市有茶馬也，分蕃有圉長也。其設官也，擬之漢唐宋，豈不爲尤密乎？今亦取其賢者而任之，取其不肖者而退之耳。旣有見馬以
translation_en:
…military service. This was the practice in the interior commanderies. The people were allowed to raise livestock without official prohibition; some accumulated a thousand horses, others several thousand. This was the practice along the frontier. Were these not institutions of the Han? For those obliged to furnish horses, the government provided the purchase price: twenty-five thousand cash per horse. Regional Inspectors, Commandants, and Vice Commandants conducted thorough inspections annually. Horses unfit for battle were sold, and the proceeds used to buy replacements; any shortfall was supplied by the garrison. This was the provision of money for purchases. As the garrison militia system gradually deteriorated, soldiers became too poor to procure horses, so they were supplied with horses from government pastures. This was the provision of horses for use. Were these not institutions of the Tang? In the Song period, there were what were called government horses, raised in government pastures; civilian horses, distributed among registered households; and military horses, purchased in frontier commanderies. These are all methods of earlier times that you wish to weigh and put into practice. Yet I, your unlearned student, simply consider this inadvisable. Why? Because the sound elements of those methods have already been adopted and put to use today, while those unsuited to present circumstances cannot be implemented.

Examining further the institutions of the present time, at the center there is the Court of the Imperial Stud, while prefectures, subprefectures, and counties appoint assistant officials specifically to oversee these matters. Outside the capital there are Regional Courts of the Imperial Stud, while the Courts of Imperial Herds establish pasture directorates and pastures to divide responsibility. For frontier trade there are Tea and Horse offices; for the division of herds [?], there are stable heads. Compared with the Han, Tang, and Song, is this arrangement of offices not even more comprehensive? All that is needed now is to appoint the worthy and dismiss the unworthy. There are already horses on hand to…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
給軍而又有寄馬以給民旣責之以牧養
而又責之以孳息印烙以防之也考課以
驗之也其立法也視之漢唐宋豈不爲尤
密乎今亦摘其弊而袪之舉其墮而興之
耳嗚呼
祖宗之法至精至備行之天下而無弊傳之萬
世而可法今馬政之未舉者則亦講求之
未明修復之未至耳豈可不責之人而惟
法之是然不究乎今而惟古之是圖哉夫
===
祖宗精備之法適我
聖天子大有爲之日碩俊簡布於
朝廷羣能分列於外服竭蹇蹇之忠秉明明
之節司太僕者寧無張萬歲其人耶司死
馬者寧無王毛仲其人耶誠一振舉於萎
薾之餘剗剔乎奸徵之弊則一綠一馬雲
錦成羣亦何難致之有哉若夫孝武上自
封君以次出馬官給牝馬歸息什一王安
punctuated: 給軍，而又有寄馬以給民；旣責之以牧養，而又責之以孳息，印烙以防之也，考課以驗之也。其立法也，視之漢唐宋，豈不爲尤密乎？今亦摘其弊而袪之，舉其墮而興之耳。嗚呼！祖宗之法至精至備，行之天下而無弊，傳之萬世而可法。今馬政之未舉者，則亦講求之未明，修復之未至耳。豈可不責之人，而惟法之是然；不究乎今，而惟古之是圖哉？夫祖宗精備之法，適我聖天子大有爲之日，碩俊簡布於朝廷，羣能分列於外服，竭蹇蹇之忠，秉明明之節。司太僕者，寧無張萬歲其人耶？司死馬者，寧無王毛仲其人耶？誠一振舉於萎薾之餘，剗剔乎奸徵之弊，則一綠一馬，雲錦成羣，亦何難致之有哉？若夫孝武，上自封君，以次出馬，官給牝馬，歸息什一，王安
translation_en:
…to supply the army, while there are also horses entrusted to the common people. Those responsible are charged both with pasturing and tending them and with breeding them. Branding provides a safeguard, and performance assessments provide verification. Compared with those of the Han, Tang, and Song, are these regulations not still more thorough? All that is needed now is to identify and remove their abuses, and to revive what has fallen into neglect. Alas! The laws of our imperial ancestors are supremely refined and complete: they can be implemented throughout the realm without ill effects and transmitted as models for ten thousand generations. If horse administration has yet to be properly carried out today, this is merely because its principles have not been clearly investigated and its restoration has not been fully accomplished. How could one fail to hold people responsible and lay the blame solely on the laws [?], or fail to investigate present conditions and concern oneself only with antiquity?

These refined and complete ancestral laws now meet an age in which our sage Son of Heaven undertakes great achievements. Eminent and talented men have been selected for service at court, and able men have been posted throughout the territorial administration. They devote themselves with unswerving loyalty and uphold conspicuously enlightened integrity. Among those directing the Court of the Imperial Stud, can there be no man like Zhang Wansui? Among those overseeing “dead horses” [?], can there be no man like Wang Maozhong? If, after this period of decline, they would truly make a concerted effort to restore affairs and eradicate the abuses of fraudulent exactions [?], how could it be difficult to achieve “one green, one horse” [?], with herds splendid as cloud-patterned brocade?

As for Emperor Xiaowu, who required contributions of horses beginning with the enfeoffed lords and proceeding down through the ranks, and had the authorities provide mares, with one-tenth of their offspring to be returned; and Wang An…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
石信曾孝寬之言恕文彥博之議卒得保
馬之法而為天下之害則漢宋之敝政不
敢屑屑為執事陳也雖然滴腸續骨醫者
之技雖妙不如不疾之為愈焦頭爛額救
者之功固多不如不焚之為貴與其畜馬
以為用不如無事而不用馬也書曰歸馬
於華山之陽此又愚生言外之望也不知
執事以為如何
第五問
貫侃
===
同考試官教諭趙　批〔就問目中處置而推本於節用愛民可觀〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔隆舉是如此必留心於世務者〕
考試官學正方　批〔整贍可錄〕
有足國之大本有強國之大本食貨者足
國之道也而其本在於節用戎兵者強國
之道也而其本在於安民用既節則國不
期足而自足民既安則國不期強而自強
punctuated:
石信曾孝寬之言，恕文彥博之議，卒得保馬之法，而為天下之害，則漢宋之敝政，不敢屑屑為執事陳也。雖然，滴腸續骨，醫者之技雖妙，不如不疾之為愈；焦頭爛額，救者之功固多，不如不焚之為貴。與其畜馬以為用，不如無事而不用馬也。《書》曰：「歸馬於華山之陽。」此又愚生言外之望也，不知執事以為如何？

第五問
貫侃

同考試官教諭趙批〔就問目中處置，而推本於節用愛民，可觀。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔隆舉是如此，必留心於世務者。〕
考試官學正方批〔整贍可錄。〕

有足國之大本，有強國之大本。食貨者，足國之道也，而其本在於節用；戎兵者，強國之道也，而其本在於安民。用既節，則國不期足而自足；民既安，則國不期強而自強。
translation_en:
…Wang Anshi trusted Zeng Xiaokuan’s words and forgave [?] Wen Yanbo’s objections, ultimately adopting the household horse-maintenance system, which brought harm upon the realm. As for these defective policies of the Han and Song, I dare not trouble you with a minute account. Nevertheless, however marvelous a physician’s skill at treating the intestines [?] and setting broken bones, it is better never to fall ill. However great the services of those who fight a fire until their heads are scorched and their foreheads burned, it is more precious to have no fire at all. Rather than raise horses for use, it would be better to have peace and no need to use them. The Book of Documents says: “He sent the horses back to the southern slopes of Mount Hua.” This, too, is the hope that your humble student cherishes beyond what he has explicitly said. I wonder what you think of it?

Fifth Policy Question
Guan Kan

Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔He addresses the matters raised in the question and traces their basis to frugality in expenditure and care for the people. Worth reading.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The treatment is thus [?]; he must be someone who pays close attention to the affairs of the age.〕
Examiner Fang, School Director, comments: 〔Orderly and ample; worthy of selection.〕

There is a fundamental basis for making the state prosperous, and a fundamental basis for making it strong. Food and wealth are the means of enriching the state, but their foundation lies in frugal expenditure. Arms and troops are the means of strengthening the state, but their foundation lies in securing the people’s well-being. Once expenditure is restrained, the state becomes prosperous of itself, without deliberately seeking prosperity. Once the people are secure, the state becomes strong of itself, without deliberately seeking strength.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
苟務國之足而不本於節用吾知所入者
不能給其所出雖頭會箕斂民力愈竭而
用益不足矣務國之强而不本於安民吾
知本既先撥而戎狄乘之良民善衆亦且
化而爲大盜矣孔子曰節用而愛人請以
是並爲明問復蓋嘗聞之洪範先食貨於
八政故知有天下者不可無財用周官列
司馬於六卿故知有天下者不可無戎兵
昔者先王因地制貢則壤成賦料丁起役
===
而食貨興矣我
國家之制既有邊儲矣復有京運存留之設
既有歲辦矣復有丁傭貨權之例其綜理
之詳雖夏后之貢成周之徹何以加焉若
是者食宜無不足也貨宜無不充也今自
山西所急而言之督併之使屢下于邊陲
告乏之疏累陳於藩室噫有由然哉輸於
邊者有常數而客兵調集每至若林之多
供乎祿者有定額而
punctuated:
苟務國之足而不本於節用，吾知所入者不能給其所出，雖頭會箕斂，民力愈竭而用益不足矣。務國之强而不本於安民，吾知本既先撥而戎狄乘之，良民善衆亦且化而爲大盜矣。孔子曰：「節用而愛人。」請以是並爲明問復。蓋嘗聞之，《洪範》先食貨於八政，故知有天下者不可無財用；《周官》列司馬於六卿，故知有天下者不可無戎兵。昔者先王因地制貢，則壤成賦，料丁起役，而食貨興矣。
我國家之制，既有邊儲矣，復有京運存留之設；既有歲辦矣，復有丁傭貨權之例。其綜理之詳，雖夏后之貢、成周之徹，何以加焉？若是者，食宜無不足也，貨宜無不充也。今自山西所急而言之，督併之使屢下于邊陲，告乏之疏累陳於藩室。噫！有由然哉！輸於邊者有常數，而客兵調集，每至若林之多；供乎祿者有定額，而
translation_en:
If one seeks to make the state prosperous without taking economy in expenditure as the foundation, I know that its income will not cover its outlay. Even if taxes are exacted by counting every head and gathering wealth by the basketful, the people's resources will become ever more exhausted, while funds for expenditure grow ever less adequate. If one seeks to make the state strong without taking the people's security as the foundation, I know that, once the foundation has been shaken, the Rong and Di will exploit the opportunity, and even decent, law-abiding people will turn into great bandits. Confucius said: “Be economical in expenditure and cherish the people.” Allow me to offer this as my answer to both parts of your discerning question. I have heard that the Great Plan places food and wealth first among the eight affairs of government; thus we know that those who possess All-under-Heaven cannot do without fiscal resources. The Offices of Zhou ranks the Minister of War among the Six Ministers; thus we know that those who possess All-under-Heaven cannot do without armed forces. In antiquity, the former kings established tribute according to local conditions, assessed taxes according to the soil, and levied labor service after reckoning the number of adult males. Thus food supplies and wealth flourished.
Under our dynasty's institutions, there are not only frontier reserves but also arrangements for transporting revenue to the capital and retaining it locally; there are not only annual procurement quotas but also regulations for payments in lieu of adult male labor service and the regulation of currency [?]. In the comprehensiveness and detail of their administration, how could even the tribute system of the Xia rulers or the che tax system of Zhou surpass them? With such arrangements, food should never be insufficient, and wealth should never be lacking. Yet, speaking now of Shanxi's pressing needs, envoys charged with enforcing collection [?] are repeatedly dispatched to the frontier, and memorials reporting shortages are repeatedly presented in the princely establishments [?]. Alas! Surely there are reasons for this! Deliveries to the frontier have fixed quotas, yet troops transferred in from elsewhere are often assembled in numbers as dense as a forest. The provision for stipends has a fixed allotment, yet…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
天潢繁衍乃有螽斯之盛況夫窮民之逋大災
傷之蠲除豪右竊攬代之權貪夫肆侵漁
之利其欲粟陳而不可食貫朽而不可較
不亦難哉為今之計者宜何如邪粟之貴
賤所當平也貴則減價以糶之賤則增價
以糴之是亦古人備荒之一策也幣之輕
重所當權也幣輕則母權子而行幣重則
子權母而行是亦古人救時之一法也今
之存積即先王積餘之意脩其廢焉非常
===
之用寧不足充乎今之預備即先王藏鏹
之意舉其墮焉不時之需寧不足給乎夫
然後時檢校以閱其實嚴刑罰以禁其奸
其庶乎食貨之可足矣雖然究其本而言
之不有節用者乎無名之賞賜有度不急
之土木不興非時之遊觀有節無益之冗
費不設如是而已耳先王威夷狄平邦國
除盜賊而戎兵興矣我
國家之制內有五府外又設衛所以分屬之
alt_text:
1: 天災繁衍乃有斂斯之感況夫窮民之逋欠以
2: 傷之蠲除豪右竊攬代之糴貪夫肆侵漁
3: 之利其欲粟陳而不可食貫朽而不可較
4: 不亦難哉為今之計者宜何如邪粟之貴
5: 賤所當平也貴則減價以糶之賤則增價
6: 以糴之是亦古人備荒之一策也幣之輕
7: 重所當權也幣輕則毋權子而行幣重則
8: 子權母而行是亦古人救時之一法也今
9: 之存積即先王積餘之意脩其廢焉非常
===
1: 之用寧不足充乎今之預備即先王蔵𥡴
2: 之意舉其墮焉不時之需寧不足給乎夫
3: 然後時檢校以閱其實嚴刑罰以禁其奸
4: 其庶乎食貨之可足矣雖然究其本而言
5: 之不有節用者乎無名之賞賜有度不急
6: 之土木不興非時之遊觀有節無益之冗
7: 費不設如是而已耳先王威夷狄平邦國
8: 除盜賊而戎兵興矣我
9: 國家之制內有五府也又設衛所以分屬之
punctuated:
天潢繁衍，乃有螽斯之盛。況夫窮民之逋大，災傷之蠲除，豪右竊攬代之權，貪夫肆侵漁之利，其欲粟陳而不可食、貫朽而不可較，不亦難哉？為今之計者，宜何如邪？粟之貴賤，所當平也。貴則減價以糶之，賤則增價以糴之，是亦古人備荒之一策也。幣之輕重，所當權也。幣輕則母權子而行，幣重則子權母而行，是亦古人救時之一法也。今之存積，即先王積餘之意，脩其廢焉，非常之用寧不足充乎？今之預備，即先王藏鏹之意，舉其墮焉，不時之需寧不足給乎？夫然後時檢校以閱其實，嚴刑罰以禁其奸，其庶乎食貨之可足矣。雖然，究其本而言之，不有節用者乎？無名之賞賜有度，不急之土木不興，非時之遊觀有節，無益之冗費不設，如是而已耳。
先王威夷狄，平邦國，除盜賊，而戎兵興矣。我國家之制，內有五府，外又設衛所以分屬之。
translation_en:
…the imperial lineage multiplies, flourishing like the prolific offspring celebrated in “The Locusts.” Consider, moreover, the mounting arrears of the impoverished [?], remissions for damage caused by disasters, powerful families usurping control over handling tax payments on others’ behalf, and greedy men freely profiting from their exactions. To wish, under these circumstances, for grain to grow too old to eat and strings of cash to rot so that the coins can no longer be counted—is this not difficult?
What, then, should be done now? Grain prices should be stabilized. When grain is dear, sell it at reduced prices; when it is cheap, buy it at increased prices. This, too, was one of the ancients’ measures for preparing against famine. The relative values of currency should be balanced. When currency is light, let the “mother,” or larger denomination, circulate to balance the “child,” or smaller denomination; when currency is heavy, let the “child” circulate to balance the “mother.” This, too, was one of the ancients’ methods for remedying the troubles of their times. Today’s accumulated reserves embody the former kings’ intention of storing surpluses. If neglected practices are restored, how could extraordinary expenditures lack sufficient provision? Today’s preparatory reserves embody the former kings’ intention of storing money. If what has fallen into disuse is revived, how could unforeseen needs lack sufficient supplies? Thereafter, conduct periodic inspections to verify the actual holdings, and enforce strict punishments to prevent fraud. Then perhaps grain and financial resources may be sufficient.
Nevertheless, to examine the matter at its root, is there not also the need to economize? Set limits on rewards bestowed without justification; undertake no construction that is not urgent; restrain excursions and sightseeing at inappropriate times; and incur no useless, excessive expenditure. That is all.
The former kings overawed the Yi and Di peoples, pacified the states, and eliminated robbers and bandits; thus military forces arose. Under our dynasty’s institutions, there are the Five Chief Military Commissions at the capital, and guards and battalions are also established outside it and assigned among them.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
外有司衛也又設將臣以總率之其經畧
之備雖商之赫業周之詰揚莫有過焉若
此者蠻夷宜率服也盜賊宜屏息也今自
近日之事而言之饑民嘯聚流劫郡縣嘗
調京軍以捕禦之乃至飄忽震蕩過無堅
城而剿之者卒賴邊軍焉是郡縣之變京
軍既不足恃矣窮虜驕縱侵竊邊關嘗有
邊軍以把戍之乃至斥突憑陵無勇將
而禦之者又調京軍焉是邊關之變邊軍
===
亦不足恃矣噫有由然哉武弁以甲胄爲
恥而慕文墨軍士以工賈爲業而惡戰鬬
况夫坐作進退之未習而卒不知兵斂斂
鍛礪之未弔而兵無完器精銳或隱於藿
門老弱多充於部伍其欲摧鋒陷敵折馘
執俘不亦難哉爲今之計者宜何如邪選
將以主兵閱卒以實伍而兵之本以立簡
器以利用演陣以教戰而兵之用以備治
渤海如龔遂長朝歌如虞詡必求是人而
punctuated:
外有司衛也，又設將臣以總率之。其經畧之備，雖商之赫業、周之詰揚，莫有過焉。若此者，蠻夷宜率服也，盜賊宜屏息也。今自近日之事而言之，饑民嘯聚，流劫郡縣，嘗調京軍以捕禦之，乃至飄忽震蕩，過無堅城，而剿之者卒賴邊軍焉。是郡縣之變，京軍既不足恃矣。窮虜驕縱，侵竊邊關，嘗有邊軍以把戍之，乃至斥突憑陵，無勇將，而禦之者又調京軍焉。是邊關之變，邊軍亦不足恃矣。
噫！有由然哉！武弁以甲胄爲恥而慕文墨，軍士以工賈爲業而惡戰鬬。况夫坐作進退之未習，而卒不知兵；斂斂鍛礪之未弔，而兵無完器。精銳或隱於藿門，老弱多充於部伍，其欲摧鋒陷敵、折馘執俘，不亦難哉！爲今之計者，宜何如邪？選將以主兵，閱卒以實伍，而兵之本以立；簡器以利用，演陣以教戰，而兵之用以備。治渤海如龔遂，長朝歌如虞詡，必求是人而
translation_en:
…outside the capital there are offices and guards [?], and military commanders are also appointed to exercise overall command. So complete are these strategic arrangements that even the glorious achievements of the Shang and the Zhou’s proclamation of military resolve did not surpass them. With arrangements such as these, the non-Chinese peoples ought all to submit, and bandits ought to cease their activities. Yet, to speak of recent events, starving people have gathered in bands and roamed about plundering prefectures and counties. Capital troops were dispatched to capture and repel them, but the raiders moved unpredictably, spreading turmoil, and no city in their path proved secure. In the end, their suppression depended upon frontier troops. Thus, in disturbances within the prefectures and counties, the capital troops have already proved unreliable. The desperate enemy, arrogant and unrestrained, has encroached upon the frontier passes. Frontier troops were stationed to guard them, yet the enemy charged in and overran them, with no brave commanders to stand against them; to repel them, capital troops were again dispatched. Thus, in disturbances along the frontier, the frontier troops have likewise proved unreliable.
Alas! Surely there are reasons for this! Military officers regard wearing armor and helmets as shameful and aspire instead to literary pursuits; soldiers make their living through crafts and commerce and detest combat. Moreover, they have not practiced sitting and rising, advancing and retreating, so the soldiers know nothing of warfare. The gathering [?], forging, and sharpening of weapons have not been attended to [?], so the troops lack serviceable equipment. Some of the best fighting men remain hidden in humble households, while the old and weak fill the ranks. Is it not difficult to expect such troops to break the enemy’s spearhead, penetrate his formations, cut off ears, and take prisoners? What measures, then, should be taken today? Select commanders to lead the troops and inspect the soldiers to fill out the ranks: thereby the foundations of the army will be established. Inspect weapons to ensure their effective use and drill formations to teach combat: thereby the army will be prepared for action. To govern Bohai as Gong Sui did, or to serve as magistrate of Zhaoge as Yu Xu did, one must seek out men of this kind and…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
任以捕盜之責備北邊如李牧守雲中如
廉范必擇是人而付以備邊之任夫然後
鼓之以慶賞震之以刑威庶乎戎兵可振
矣雖然究其本而言之不有安民者乎生
之而不傷厚之而不困扶之而不危節其
力而不盡如是而已耳稽之於古度官祿
量國用以徵其租出口錢計筭錢以課其
丁或至三十稅一者漢之取民可謂寬矣
而文景乃有海內庶富之效田有租家有
===
調丁有儒既以為經常之制量事宜度災
變差老少又以為減除之權或至課役皆
免者唐之取民可謂輕矣而太宗乃有斗
米三錢之效此漢唐食貨之大略也府兵
之制不為不善而卒致藩鎮之禍番府兵
之制壞而彍騎之兵興彍騎之兵變而藩
鎮之權重至其末年朝廷行姑息之政強
將擁不制之兵而唐亡矣衛府之兵不為
不密而卒致金虜之變者藩鎮之權失而
punctuated:
任以捕盜之責。備北邊如李牧，守雲中如廉范，必擇是人而付以備邊之任。夫然後鼓之以慶賞，震之以刑威，庶乎戎兵可振矣。雖然，究其本而言之，不有安民者乎？生之而不傷，厚之而不困，扶之而不危，節其力而不盡，如是而已耳。
稽之於古，度官祿，量國用，以徵其租；出口錢，計筭錢，以課其丁，或至三十稅一者，漢之取民可謂寬矣，而文景乃有海內庶富之效。田有租，家有調，丁有儒，既以為經常之制；量事宜，度災變，差老少，又以為減除之權，或至課役皆免者，唐之取民可謂輕矣，而太宗乃有斗米三錢之效。此漢唐食貨之大略也。
府兵之制不為不善，而卒致藩鎮之禍。番府兵之制壞，而彍騎之兵興；彍騎之兵變，而藩鎮之權重。至其末年，朝廷行姑息之政，強將擁不制之兵，而唐亡矣。衛府之兵不為不密，而卒致金虜之變者，藩鎮之權失而
translation_en:
…entrust them with responsibility for apprehending bandits. To defend the northern frontier as Li Mu did, or to guard Yunzhong as Lian Fan did, one must select men of this kind and entrust them with frontier defense. Only then should one encourage them with rewards and overawe them with the威力 of punishments; thus there may be hope of revitalizing the armed forces. Yet, speaking of the root of the matter, does it not lie in bringing peace to the people? Sustain them without harming them, enrich them without impoverishing them, support them without endangering them, and use their strength sparingly without exhausting it: that is all.
Examining antiquity, the Han assessed officials’ salaries and estimated state expenditure to determine the collection of land taxes; they levied the population tax and calculated the poll tax to assess adult males. The land-tax rate sometimes fell to one-thirtieth: the Han’s exactions from the people may indeed be called lenient. Under Emperors Wen and Jing, this produced a populous and prosperous realm. Under the Tang, fields owed land tax, households owed household tax, and adult males owed labor service [?; the transcription reads 儒]. These were established as regular institutions. Yet the authorities also considered circumstances, assessed calamities, and distinguished the old from the young, exercising discretion to reduce or remit obligations, sometimes exempting people entirely from taxes and service. The Tang’s exactions from the people may indeed be called light. Under Emperor Taizong, this produced the result that a dou of rice cost only three cash. Such is a broad outline of food supply and finance under the Han and Tang.
The system of militia units was by no means ill conceived, yet it ultimately led to the calamity of the regional military commands. When the system of militia units collapsed [?; an unclear 番 precedes this clause], the Expanded Cavalry forces arose; when those forces changed, the power of the regional military commands grew. In the dynasty’s final years, the court pursued a policy of appeasement, while powerful generals commanded troops beyond its control, and the Tang fell. The forces of the guards and military headquarters were by no means loosely organized, yet they ultimately brought about the catastrophe inflicted by the Jin invaders. This occurred because authority over the regional military commands was lost, and…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
兵始弱保甲之法行而民始困至其末年
主之以非人用之以妖術而宋危矣此唐
宋戎兵之大略也或始焉粗備而僅致小
康或終焉不戰而卒成大禍漢唐宋之所
以爲漢唐宋也如此曷足以爲當時法而
執事陳哉
punctuated: 兵始弱，保甲之法行而民始困。至其末年，主之以非人，用之以妖術，而宋危矣。此唐宋戎兵之大略也。或始焉粗備而僅致小康，或終焉不戰而卒成大禍，漢唐宋之所以爲漢唐宋也如此，曷足以爲當時法而執事陳哉？
translation_en: …the army began to weaken; when the baojia system of mutual responsibility was implemented, the people began to suffer hardship. In its final years, unsuitable men were put in command, and sorcery was employed, bringing the Song into peril. Such is a broad outline of military affairs under the Tang and Song. In some cases, preparations were rudimentary at the outset and achieved only modest stability; in others, failure to fight ultimately brought great calamity. Such were the circumstances that made the Han, Tang, and Song what they were. How could these suffice as models for the present age and merit presentation to you, honored examiners?

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
正德癸酉開科取士
聖明繼統之八年也山西列郡之
士顒顒昂昂起應時需及鎖
院環棘主司登明選公益極
其精監察御史周〔倫〕綱維內
外統紀嚴密論秀於一千三
===
百人中而得士六十有五隋
珠和璧可多得乎哉故事有
錄以
獻〔謙〕叨厠校文敢僭序於末簡
夫人才國家之利器而所以
用之不乏者視所以養之何
如耳三代之時教法寖備人
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

正德癸酉，開科取士，聖明繼統之八年也。山西列郡之士顒顒昂昂，起應時需。及鎖院環棘，主司登明選公，益極其精。監察御史周〔倫〕綱維內外，統紀嚴密，論秀於一千三百人中，而得士六十有五。隋珠和璧，可多得乎哉？故事，有錄以獻。〔謙〕叨厠校文，敢僭序於末簡。

夫人才，國家之利器，而所以用之不乏者，視所以養之何如耳。三代之時，教法寖備，人
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of the Zhengde reign [1513], an examination was held to select scholars. This was the eighth year since our sagacious sovereign succeeded to the throne. The scholars of Shanxi’s prefectures, dignified and high-spirited, arose to answer the needs of the time. Once the examination compound was locked and enclosed with thorn branches, the presiding examiners advanced the worthy and selected impartially, exercising the utmost discernment. Investigating Censor Zhou Lun 周倫 maintained order within and without, enforcing strict and meticulous discipline. From among thirteen hundred candidates, sixty-five were selected for their outstanding qualities. Could treasures such as the pearl of Sui and the jade of He be obtained in great numbers? Following established practice, a record was compiled for presentation to the throne. I, Qian 謙, having undeservedly participated in judging the examination essays, venture to append this postface to its final leaves.

Men of talent are the potent instruments of the state. Whether there is an unfailing supply of them for service depends simply on how they are nurtured. During the Three Dynasties, methods of instruction gradually became fully developed, and men…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
才傑出降及春秋子產不毁
鄉校而後世賢之則當時列
國之君教化陵夷可想見矣
漢唐而下政有汙隆教養之
法有可議者宜其人才之不
古若也今之國學鄉學比隆
往古至於懸科設彀必通經
===
學古斯爲入格而非予奪於
詩賦聲病之末度越漢唐遠
矣士之得舉於鄉者亦榮矣
哉然人之才質殊科而所就
頓異顧其所以用我者何如
而行吾用世之志其感爲僕
應有不可以强同者今
punctuated: 才傑出。降及春秋，子產不毁鄉校，而後世賢之，則當時列國之君教化陵夷，可想見矣。漢唐而下，政有汙隆，教養之法有可議者，宜其人才之不古若也。今之國學、鄉學，比隆往古；至於懸科設彀，必通經學古，斯爲入格，而非予奪於詩賦聲病之末，度越漢唐遠矣。士之得舉於鄉者，亦榮矣哉！然人之才質殊科，而所就頓異，顧其所以用我者何如，而行吾用世之志，其感爲僕應有不可以强同者。今
translation_en:
…outstanding talent emerged. By the Spring and Autumn period, Zichan did not demolish the local schools, and later generations praised him as worthy for this. One can thus imagine how far the rulers of the various states at that time had allowed moral instruction to decline. From the Han and Tang onward, government had its declines and its flourishing periods, and the methods of educating and nurturing talent were open to criticism. It is understandable that the men of talent produced did not equal those of antiquity.

Today, the national and local schools rival the flourishing institutions of antiquity. As for establishing examination categories and setting standards for selection, candidates must understand the Classics and study antiquity before they qualify. Acceptance or rejection does not rest on such trifles as tonal faults in poetry and rhapsodies. This far surpasses the Han and Tang. How glorious it is, too, for scholars to be selected in the Provincial Examination!

Yet people differ in their talents and native capacities, and their attainments differ markedly. Each must consider how he is employed and carry out his aspiration to serve the world. In their responses and service [?], there must be differences that cannot be forcibly made uniform. Now…

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:
明明天子恭默思道寤寐英賢士
之奮庸以茅斯拔因千載之
遇也爾諸士盡圖報稱而嚴
於義利公私之辯君子小人
之分始於誠身終於澤物正
其誼不謀其利明其道不計
其功上不負
===
天子下不負所學此君子之道也
若徒誦數是力纂組是誇狥
利忘義而乾沒無間是誠小
人之歸也二者其端甚微而
相去遂遠可不審哉〔謙懼知〕
人之惟難而幸遭逢之不偶
故昌言之庸以賛其成
punctuated:
明明天子恭默思道，寤寐英賢。士之奮庸，以茅斯拔，因千載之遇也。爾諸士盡圖報稱，而嚴於義利公私之辯、君子小人之分，始於誠身，終於澤物，正其誼不謀其利，明其道不計其功，上不負天子，下不負所學，此君子之道也。
若徒誦數是力，纂組是誇，狥利忘義，而乾沒無間，是誠小人之歸也。二者其端甚微，而相去遂遠，可不審哉？〔謙懼知〕人之惟難，而幸遭逢之不偶，故昌言之，庸以賛其成。
translation_en:
…the illustrious Son of Heaven reverently contemplates the Way in silence, yearning for worthy and talented men waking and sleeping. Scholars rise to service, drawn forth like clumps of thatch grass, through an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years. All you scholars should strive to repay this favor fittingly, rigorously distinguishing righteousness from profit, public from private interests, and the gentleman from the petty man. Begin by making yourselves sincere and culminate in extending benefits to others. Uphold righteousness without seeking profit; illuminate the Way without calculating success. Above, do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, do not fail what you have learned. This is the way of the gentleman.
If, however, you exert yourselves merely in recitation and counting texts, boast of weaving ornate phrases, pursue profit and forget righteousness, and grasp at gain without restraint, this is truly the path toward becoming a petty man. The initial distinction between these two courses is exceedingly subtle, yet they eventually diverge far apart. Can you fail to examine this carefully? 〔I humbly fear [?] how〕 difficult it is to know men, yet count myself fortunate in this uncommon encounter [?]. Thus I speak openly, to help bring their achievement to fulfillment.

title: 正德八年山西鄉試錄
text:

學教諭劉譓謹序
